items.title: [Audit] What a player can actually do: one of thirteen systems does observable work, and the shortest path to a loop
items.body:
An end-to-end reachability audit traced from the real composition root (`src/main.ts`) outward, not from the tests. **This question is not answered anywhere else in the repository**, and the answer is short.

Claims are **VERIFIED** (read and/or executed) or **INFERRED**. Executed claims were driven through `createNewSimulationRuntime` and `Kernel.step()` — the same runtime the worker builds — from throwaway scripts outside the repository. Raw output is quoted.

---

## 1. What a player can do today

1. **Load the page and look at an empty grey world.** The worker is `uninitialized`; the strip reads `Day --` and zeros.
2. **Press "New prison".** The only thing on the page that starts a simulation. You get a 32×32 square of dirt with one owned chunk, and a save.
3. **Look at the prison.** Pan with the middle button, WASD or arrows; zoom with wheel, `+`, `−`; one-finger drag and two-finger pinch on touch. **Nothing the camera does reaches the simulation.**
4. **Start and stop time.** Pause / Play / Fast-forward genuinely work. One in-game day is two minutes of real time at ×1.
5. **Switch to Build and choose "Brick wall" or "Wooden door".** The only two entries.
6. **Press "Place on map", then click or drag along a tile edge.** A translucent brown box appears. It is a build *order*.
7. **Watch that box stay translucent forever.** It never becomes a wall — there is no way in the entire interface to buy the bricks it waits for. It survives every save and reload.
8. **Type coordinates instead.** Same outcome. **A coordinate outside the owned chunk is silently discarded** — nothing appears and nothing says why.
9. **Save, load, delete, export.** All work. Export downloads a file the application cannot import back.
10. **`?actors=demo`** shows three scripted sprites walking in a circle. A rendering demonstration, not simulation state.

**That is the complete list.** The single mechanical consequence a player can produce is item 6: a ghost outline.

---

## 2. The proof, executed

`createNewSimulationRuntime(0)`, one `PlaceBuildOrder` exactly as `main.ts` builds it at tile (16,16), then 2,000 ticks — 100 in-game seconds:

```
[A] after 2000 ticks state=materials-pending progress=0 failReason=undefined
[A] treasury=25000
[A] chunk topEdge=[[0,1024]]
```

`[[0,1024]]` is 1,024 run-length-encoded zeroes: **no wall anywhere in the world.**

The same runtime with one `PurchaseMaterials` command inserted first:

```
[B] state=completed treasury=24600
[B] chunk topEdge=[[0,528],[1,1],[0,495]]
```

Index 528 = `16 × 32 + 16` — the exact tile. **The construction pipeline is complete and correct; the only missing link in the whole chain is a producer for one command.**

---

## 3. Thirteen systems run every tick. One does work a player can see.

Read from a live runtime's `systemExecutionOrder`:

| System | Iterates | Non-empty in a reachable session? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prisoners.intake` | live prisoner entities | **No** — `admitPrisoner` has no caller in `src/` |
| `prisoners.needs-decay` | same | **No** (see #259) |
| **`construction`** | `orderedOrders()` | **Yes — the one reachable system.** Stalls at `materials-pending` |
| `procurement` | `this.pending` | **No** — returns on line 156 every tick, 20 times a second, forever |
| `navigation` | graph + queue | **Partially.** `ensureGraph()` does real work; **nothing reads its output** — no route is ever requested |
| `prisoners.actions` | prisoner query | No |
| `operations.jobs` | `activeJobs()` | **No** — `submitCarryItem` has no caller |
| `contraband.intelligence` | decays an empty ledger | No |
| `security.deployment` | `allGuardIds()` | **No** — `GuardRoster.hire` has no caller |
| `security.patrol` | same | No |
| `incidents.trigger` | `sectorIds` (empty) | No |
| `contraband.search` | queued orders (none) | No |
| `incidents.response` | `openIncidents()` | No |

**Eleven of thirteen iterate permanently empty collections.** One more does real computation nothing reads.

### Three subsystems are not even registered

- **`TopologyManager`** (229 lines) is constructed, exposed on `SimulationRuntime.topology`, and **`update()` is never called anywhere in `src/`**. It has no `id`/`order`/`schedule`, **so it cannot be registered with the kernel at all.** Room enclosure detection never runs.
- **`UtilityNetwork`** — two instances built, no `update`, and `addNode`/`connect`/`evaluate` have no caller outside their own module.
- **`ContainerRegistry`, `JobBoard`, `JobWorkerPool`** — built empty; only the construction container is registered and nothing is ever put in it.

---

## 4. Three findings worth their own attention

### A finished wooden door writes nothing and creates no door

`edgeNumericIdFor` returns `0` for `category: 'object'`, so `finalizeConstruction` only bumps the geometry revision. Executed:

```
[C] door state=completed
[C] topEdge=[[0,1024]]  leftEdge=[[0,1024]]
```

It exists only as a 0.55-tile-high brown slab drawn from the order list. `DoorRegistry.register` is called from exactly one place — restoring from a snapshot. **Nothing creates the first door.**

### A refused order gives the player no feedback of any kind

The command reply acknowledges *receipt*, not effect: `state-machine.ts:524-535` posts `status: 'queued'` as soon as the kernel accepts it. A `failReason` of `out-of-bounds` or `unowned-land` is mapped to `undefined` by `phaseOf` and drawn as nothing. Executed, typing `100, 100` into fields that have no `min`/`max`:

```
[E] far order state=failed failReason=out-of-bounds
```

The refusal line stays hidden because the command *was* queued successfully, and no ghost appears. (`x = 2e9`, `x = -5`, `x = 9e12` all fail cleanly — **no player-reachable crash was found down any path.**)

### `ConstructionSystem` has a complete undo/redo model that nothing can reach

`undo()`/`redo()` are transaction-grouped and snapshot-safe; `main.ts:492` mints one `transactionId` per gesture *specifically* so a twelve-segment wall undoes as one. There is no control, no binding and no intent that can trigger it — `grep` for `KeyZ`, `ctrlKey`, `metaKey` in `src/` returns **zero matches**.

Five of six commands have no producer: `PurchaseMaterials`, `CancelBuildOrder`, `Undo`, `Redo`, `ZoneRoom` — and `ZoneRoom`'s consumer is itself a no-op (`case 'ZoneRoom': break;`).

---

## 5. Where each on-screen number comes from

Fresh session, before any tick:

```
[D] {"prisoners":0,"prisonersInIntake":0,"prisonersHighRisk":0,"staff":0,
     "staffUnassigned":0,"rooms":0,"roomCapacity":0,"roomOccupants":0,
     "activeIncidents":0,"contrabandDiscovered":0,"treasuryMinorUnits":25000}
```

| On screen | Real or constant? |
| --- | --- |
| **Prisoners** | Real projection, **permanently 0** |
| Cell occupancy bar | **Never rendered** — `prisonerCapacity` is hard-coded `0` on the main thread, so the bar is removed |
| **Staff** / **Rooms** / **Incidents** / **Contraband** | Real projections, all permanently 0 |
| **Funds** | Real value, **effectively a constant 25,000** — nothing credits it and the only spender is unreachable |
| **Day N** and **% through the day** | **Real and moving.** The only figures that change |
| **Alerts** | **Always "No active alerts."** `viewModel.alerts` is assigned nowhere except a literal `[]` |
| **Minimap** | **Constant string** "Minimap is not available yet" |
| **World canvas** | Real. **Actors are always empty** — the feed's own comment says the bundle *does* carry prisoner tile positions and this feed does not decode them |

**Two projections produce nothing anyone reads:** `projectWorldForRendering` has no consumer at all — the renderer decodes the *save bundle's* world section instead, so the purpose-built render projection is dead and the save format is doing its job. And `projectStatusStrip`'s `clock` and `regime` blocks are computed and discarded.

---

## 6. The built/reachable line, measured

**207 of 256 `.ts` files under `src/` are reachable from the composition root; 49 are not.** Excluding barrels, the 29 substantive never-imported modules total **3,978 lines**: all of `services/telemetry/`, `services/entitlements/`, `services/challenges/`, `persistence/cloud/`, and three presentation projections.

**Reachable-but-never-called exports**, each verified by grep: `TopologyManager.update`, `admitPrisoner`, `GuardRoster.hire`, `JobBoard.submitCarryItem`, `UtilityNetwork.addNode/connect/evaluate`, `resolveEscapeOpportunity`, `buildRiotRegimeSchedule`, `toIncidentAlert`, `summarizeIncidents`, nine of the ten presentation projections, `remapKeyboardBinding`, `saveInputSettings`, `loadAccessibilitySettings`, `SessionController.importInto`.

**Content:** 62 declared ids, **53 with no reference in `src/` outside `src/content/`**. The nine that have one are all referenced by a system that never runs on live data. Zero contraband categories, zero security grades, zero staff roles and zero object ids are referenced from `src/` at all.

**One unused message key:** `HUD_MESSAGE_KEY.buildNote` is declared and never rendered — the only one of 56 with no render site. Its English is *"An order is queued now and built while the clock runs."* Given §2, it is fortunate it is not on screen.

---

## 7. The shortest path to a playable loop, ordered

Wiring only. No new architecture, no ADR, no new abstraction.

**Step 1 — Make a placed wall become a wall.** The highest-value change in the repository; everything downstream is proven to work. **The owner has chosen the surface: a quantity stepper on the Build panel** (not the auto-purchase this audit first sketched). That work is in flight. What the player gets: the ghost turns solid, and the **Funds** chip drops. Two of six status numbers start moving. It also makes insolvency visible — 25,000 buys 156 walls, and `spend` refuses rather than overdrawing — which leads straight to step 2.

**Step 2 — Tell the player when the simulation refuses.** Without it, "out of money" is indistinguishable from today's bug. Two facts currently vanish: `PurchaseOutcome` is discarded at `session-commands.ts:42` (the code says so), and `failReason` never leaves the simulation. The machinery already exists and has **never had a producer**: `HudViewModel.alerts` is fully implemented, with severity badges and an empty-state row. Publish a small refusal field on the existing `simulation/status-counts` channel — no new message kind — and map it in `main.ts`'s existing listener.

**Step 3 — Make `ZoneRoom` register a room instance.** Its handler is `break;`. `RoomInstanceRegistry.register` takes exactly what the command carries plus a capacity and capability list. **Do this before step 4:** `IntakeSystem` marks an arrival `'failed'` when no instance of the required room type exists *at all*, so admitting into a prison with no cell is a structural dead end, not a wait.

**Step 4 — Admit one prisoner.** Executed proof that the rest is ready — one `room.cell` registered, `admitPrisoner` called, 600 ticks:

```
entity=0 intakeStage=4 (completed)
metrics={"completedCount":1,"failedCount":0,"accommodationBacklogTicks":0}
counts={"prisoners":1,...,"rooms":1,"roomCapacity":1,"roomOccupants":1,...}
position=10,10  (the cell's anchor tile)
```

**Two calls turn three of the six status numbers real.** Fix #259 in the same change, or the prisoner is inert.

**Step 5 — Decode actors into the render frame.** `actors: []` is one line, and the feed's comment says the data is already in the bundle. `ActorLayer` is built, the atlases load, and `DemoActorFeed` proves the sprite path end to end. **This is the moment the prison stops being a diagram.**

**Step 6 — Reach the undo that already exists.** A binding plus a case, and a fully built feature returns.

---

## What is deliberately not claimed

- The page was not run in a browser. Every DOM/Phaser statement is from source and marked INFERRED; every simulation statement marked VERIFIED was executed.
- A passing test was never treated as evidence a player can reach something. Where a test is the only consumer, that is what is said.
- **No player-visible consequence is attributed to any unreachable subsystem.** `TopologyManager` never running, telemetry being unwired and 53 unconsumed ids cost a player nothing *today* — precisely because there is no loop for them to be part of. The finding is the gap between built and reachable, not an invented symptom.

items.title: A completed door can be painted as a full-tile opaque slab, because a stale edge layer defeats the guard at tile-layer.ts:488
items.body:
Found while drafting ADR 0097 (#1022, PR #1025) and **deliberately not fixed there** — an ADR pass is not the place for it. Filed separately so it is not lost inside a design document, and because the PR that landed the ADR says it was filed.

`main` @ `6180645` (v0.0.500-ish, after #1024).

## VERIFIED, read — the guard

`src/rendering/phaser/tile-layer.ts:488`, quoted exactly:

```ts
if (isDrawnAsWorldEdge(structure) && edgeTileXs.has(structure.tileX)) continue;
```

Its own comment, immediately above (`:481-487`), says what it is for:

> A finished wall or door is already on screen: the world's edge layers carry it and the loop above drew it. Its build order is still in the construction snapshot, and drawing that too puts a full-tile block under a wall that is a fifth of a tile deep. Guarded on the row really having an edge on that tile, so a save that predates #74 — completed orders, no edge values — still gets its walls.

So the guard is **conjunctive**: it skips the construction slab only when the structure is edge-drawn **and** the edge layer already carries an edge on that tile row.

## The defect — LIVE, and a code-path argument rather than a reproduction

`edgeTileXs` is derived from the world geometry the renderer currently holds. Since ADR 0040 slice 1 that geometry arrives only on a `dirty` mark or a **30-second** consistency poll, and **none of the five `dirty` triggers can fire on a build order completing** — they are, every one of them, facts about a message rather than about the simulation (`src/rendering/feed/simulation-snapshot-feed.ts`, the five `this.dirty = true` sites at `:243`, `:279`, `:304`, `:311`, `:361`; independently counted with `grep -c 'this.dirty = true'` → **5**).

So there is a window, up to 30 seconds wide, in which:

- the door is **complete** in the simulation and in the construction snapshot,
- the renderer's edge layer does **not** yet carry its edge value,
- therefore `edgeTileXs.has(structure.tileX)` is **false**,
- therefore the guard does not fire,
- therefore `paintSlab` runs for a completed structure — and `alphaFor(structure.phase)` for a completed phase is full opacity, **not** the translucent construction ghost.

**The player sees a finished door drawn as a solid full-tile block.**

## Why this is worth its own issue rather than a line in the ADR

It is the **sharper branch** of a window that was already known. `docs/research/2026-08-29-playtest-ordering-and-the-second-room.md` §7 hypothesised the same staleness mechanism for walls and measured a **9.7-second** window, and `tests/browser/playtest-harness.ts:431-434` carries it as a working comment beside a twelve-attempt retry loop. The known symptom was *"the world has not caught up yet"*. This is different in kind: the guard that exists specifically to prevent double-drawing is **defeated** by the staleness, so the wrong thing is drawn rather than the right thing arriving late.

It also explains #1018's one observation that had **no diagnosis at all**: a door still drawn as a construction block after `waitForQueueEmpty` reported empty and the Rooms panel reported ready. ADR 0097 §6 rules out the other candidate reading — `PENDING_BUILD_ORDER_STATES` (`src/simulation/construction/construction-projection.ts:86-92`) counts all five unfinished states, so the queue readout `0 waiting · 0 being built` was truthful.

## Candidate fix, not a decision

**Mark the feed dirty when the construction snapshot's completed set grows.** That is a sixth `dirty` trigger and it is the first one that would be a fact about the simulation rather than about a message — which is precisely why it deserves reading against `simulation-snapshot-feed.ts`'s own reasoning before it is written, rather than being added because it is convenient.

## The test that should have caught it, and why it did not

No browser test asserts what a *completed* structure is drawn as; `tests/browser/playtest-harness.ts` retries around the window instead of asserting on it, which is what a harness should do and is also why nothing failed. **The gate that would catch it is an assertion that a structure reported complete is not drawn with construction-phase geometry** — and it needs the LFS art bytes, which this container does not have (state 4 of `docs/AGENT_WORKFLOW.md` §2).

## Weakest claim, named

**This is a code-path argument, not a reproduction.** The feed was not instrumented and #1018's act 8 was not re-run. What is established is that the guard is conjunctive, that `edgeTileXs` comes from geometry on the 30-second channel, and that no `dirty` trigger fires on completion. What is *not* established is a measured instance of the opaque slab — #1018's screenshot pair shows a construction block, which is consistent with this and also with the simpler "not caught up yet" reading. **The reproduction is the first thing to do here.**

## Does this need an ADR?

**No.** ADR 0097 already settled the surrounding question and the owner accepted option A. This is a defect inside the mechanism that ADR describes, and its fix is a sixth trigger or an equivalent — an implementation choice, argued in the code.

items.title: [HUD] `roomOccupants` reaches nobody — the one number that separates "twelve on the roster" from "three being paid for"
items.body:
Found by playing, while settling #601. **The confusion this field would have prevented is exactly the confusion #601 is.**

## The finding

`roomOccupants` is computed (`src/simulation/presentation/status-strip-projection.ts:406-417`), is a required field on the protocol (`src/simulation/protocol/types.ts:671`), crosses the worker boundary every publication — and **has no reader anywhere outside `src/simulation/`.**

Verified here:

```
$ grep -rn 'roomOccupants' src/ | grep -v '^src/simulation/'
        (no output)
```

`src/ui/simulation-counts.ts` maps `accommodationCapacity` to `prisonerCapacity` and drops `roomOccupants` entirely. The translator's own comment explains at length why it prefers `accommodationCapacity` over `roomCapacity`; it says nothing about `roomOccupants`.

## Why it matters more than "another field with no reader"

A player who admits twelve prisoners into a prison with three beds sees **twelve** on the status strip. Nine of them are permanently parked at accommodation-assignment and **earn nothing** — income is paid per resident of a room instance, at `300 × residents`. The number that would tell them apart is computed, transmitted, and thrown away at the boundary.

That is not hypothetical: a session measured four prisons and eight day boundaries to work out why a twelve-prisoner prison was paying like a three-prisoner one, and the answer was on the wire the whole time.

## Two related observations from the same session

**The occupancy bar cannot show over-capacity at all.** `hud.status.occupancy-value` ("12 of 3") is written to `aria-valuetext` only — `src/ui/primitives/segmented-bar.ts:90-112` — so it is spoken and never shown. The bar's children are ten empty spans and `filledSegments` takes the `value >= max` branch, so **four times over capacity draws identically to exactly at capacity**.

**The Intake panel already gets this right**, and is the reason the prison was diagnosable at all: it says *"9 waiting with no bed to sleep in"*, which is correct and specific. So the copy exists; it is the status strip that is silent.

## Not claimed

No impact on a player is claimed beyond the above — nobody plays this yet. This is a field with no reader plus a bar that cannot draw its own over-capacity state, both verified by reading and by driving the interface.

## Related

#601 (the measurement this explains), #585 (an occupied place must mean a bed that currently exists — the same invariant from the payment side), #557 (fields with no reader, and why they must not all be swept up together — some carry live values, others carry values that cannot move; `roomOccupants` is firmly in the first group).

[Hygiene] 100 remote branches are fully merged into main and can be deleted — the automation token has no delete permission
items.body:
`main` is at `v0.0.37` (`d2596ad`). There are no open pull requests.

> **Corrected.** This issue first said 31 branches were deletable and 92 were unmerged. Both figures were wrong. The working clone was **shallow**, and `git branch -r --no-merged` cannot see past a graft boundary, so it reported every branch whose merge base had been cut off as unmerged. After `git fetch --unshallow` the repository shows 602 commits on `main` instead of 133, and the real split is **100 merged, 22 unmerged**. The 31 originally listed are a subset of the 100. Acting on the first version of this issue would have left 69 deletable branches behind.

## What was verified

Each of the 100 branches below was checked individually with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main`. All 100 passed, zero exceptions — their commits are already in `main`, so deleting the ref discards nothing. None is the head of an open pull request (there are none). Nothing under `origin/archive/` is included.

Most are unreachable from `main`'s tip because their PRs were **squash-merged**: the content landed, the original commit objects did not, which is exactly why the tips need deleting by hand.

## What blocks the deletion

`git push origin --delete <branch>` fails from the automation environment:

```
error: RPC failed; HTTP 403 curl 22 The requested URL returned error: 403
send-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet
```

The token available to the session can push branches but cannot delete them. This needs someone with delete rights, from a local clone or the branch list in the web UI.

## Recommended command

Do not paste the list below — recompute it, so anything merged since this issue was filed is included too. **`--unshallow` matters**; without it the same undercount recurs.

```sh
git fetch --unshallow 2>/dev/null || git fetch origin
git fetch origin --prune
git branch -r --merged origin/main \
  | sed 's#^ *origin/##' \
  | grep -v '^main$' | grep -v '^archive/' | grep -v ' -> ' \
  | xargs -n1 git push origin --delete
```

items.title: [Presentation] Finish the worker→main projection channel: two projections got special cases, the other seven the UI still cannot reach
items.body:
> **Correction — 2026-08-24.** Re-measured against `main` at `9b6965a` (v0.0.16). The core of this issue holds — there is still no general `simulation/delta` channel and most of the read-model layer is still unreachable — but **three specific claims below were false and have been corrected or deleted:**
>
> - *"Nothing outside that directory imports any of it… `grep -rn "from.*presentation" --include=*.ts src/` returns no hit from outside `src/simulation/presentation/` itself. Its only consumers are its own tests."* — **deleted; there are three importers**, all added since this was filed: `src/ui/simulation-clock.ts:1` (`projectClockPosition`), `src/simulation/worker/status-counts.ts:1` (`projectStatusStrip`) and `src/simulation/worker/state-machine.ts:14` (`HUD_VIEW_MODEL_SCHEMA_VERSION`, a constant rather than a projection).
> - *"`simulation/delta` … has no schema and no sender."* — **half false, corrected in place.** The schema exists: `src/simulation/protocol/types.ts:400-420` defines `deltaMessageSchema` with a `superRefine` enforcing `tick > baseTick`, and it is in the union at `:576`. **No sender remains true**, and that is the actual remainder.
> - The *"the HUD paints literal zeros"* quote citing `src/ui/hud/view-model.ts:131-136` — **deleted; false at that location and in substance.** That block is now `EMPTY_HUD_VIEW_MODEL` at `:207-213`, documented at `:196-206` as the deliberate first-paint default before a session exists, not what the HUD paints once one is running.
>
> The count in the title and in "The gap" was also stale: **10 files / ~2,349 lines → 11 files / 2,446 lines.** Everything else is as filed, including the whole "failure mode to design against" section, which is untouched by all of this.

The single highest-value next piece of engineering work, arrived at independently four times this session. It is small, it unblocks a large amount of already-written and already-tested code, and almost every product feature worth building is downstream of it.

## The gap

`src/simulation/presentation/` contains **11 files, 2,446 lines** of read models: `status-strip-projection.ts`, `prisoner-projection.ts`, `staff-projection.ts`, `room-projection.ts`, `security-projection.ts`, `contraband-projection.ts`, `incident-projection.ts`, `world-projection.ts`, `clock-projection.ts`, `view-model.ts`, `index.ts`.

**Two of the nine projection modules are now reachable; the other seven are not.** Measured on `main` at `9b6965a` by resolving every exported `project*` function against `src/`:

| Reachable from outside the directory | By what |
| --- | --- |
| `clock-projection.ts` — `projectClockPosition` | `src/ui/simulation-clock.ts:1`, over the `simulation/clock-state` message (PR #94) |
| `status-strip-projection.ts` — `projectStatusStrip` | `src/simulation/worker/status-counts.ts:1`, over the `simulation/status-counts` message |

| Reached by nothing in `src/` | Exported projections |
| --- | --- |
| `prisoner-projection.ts` | `projectPrisonerRoster`, `projectPrisonerPopulationCounts`, `projectPrisonerDetail` |
| `room-projection.ts` | `projectRoomList`, `projectRoomDetail` |
| `incident-projection.ts` | `projectIncidents`, `projectIncidentDetail` |
| `security-projection.ts` | `projectSecurity` |
| `staff-projection.ts` | `projectStaff` |
| `contraband-projection.ts` | `projectContraband` |
| `world-projection.ts` | `projectWorldForRendering` |

**Eleven of the thirteen exported projection functions are called from nowhere outside `src/simulation/presentation/`.** Their only other consumers are their own tests. (The two remaining hits a plain `grep` finds for `projectContraband` and `projectStatusStrip` elsewhere in `src/` — `src/content/simulation-message-keys.ts:328` and `src/simulation/prisoners/regime.ts:34` — are prose inside comments, not calls.)

The two that *are* reachable arrived as **two separate special cases**, which is the second pattern this issue was filed to prevent. There is still no general channel.

The rest is not merely unwired — it is **structurally unreachable**. The projections take live simulation state (registries, entity stores), so they can only run inside the worker; and no worker→main message carries their output. `simulation/delta` is declared in the message-kind union (`src/simulation/protocol/types.ts:22`) and now **has a schema** (`:400-420`, in the union at `:576`) — but still **no sender**, which is the whole remaining gap.

`status-strip-projection.ts:45-48` computes the HUD's counts from exactly the sources the HUD wants:

```ts
readonly prisoners: PrisonerProjectionSource;
readonly rooms?: RoomProjectionSource;
readonly staff?: StaffRosterSource;
readonly incidents?: StatusStripIncidentSource;
```

Two halves of one pipe, with a special case in place of the pipe.

## Four independent arrivals at the same conclusion

1. PR #94's own "left unsolved" section: *"The HUD's counts are still all zero. Only the clock has a publication route… That wants a real `simulation/delta` channel rather than a second special case."* — the second special case has since been built (`status-counts`), which makes this point sharper, not weaker.
2. This session's dead-code sweep, which identified `src/simulation/presentation/` as the largest test-only tree in the repository and established the structural reason.
3. A genre/retention research pass, which ranked it recommendation **#1**, effort **S**, dependencies **none** — *"This is the first thing that should be built."*
4. A browser-product research pass, which ranked the same thing #4 and noted it **blocks the three product features below it**.

## Why it is cheap

The projections were written for this. `docs/HUD_PROJECTIONS.md` contracts 1–3 already require them to be readonly, deterministically ordered, and to carry ids and message keys rather than text. Readonly and structurally-clone-safe is *exactly* what a `postMessage` boundary needs, so there is no new serialization layer to design — and no localization work either, because ADR 0011 already keeps translated text out of simulation state.

The receiving half exists too: `src/ui/hud/projection.ts` and `status-strip.ts` already map a counts view model to icons, message keys and tones.

PR #94 has already set the precedent for the protocol shape, including the ADR 0003 amendment for an unsolicited publication that does not pretend to be a request response. This channel should follow that precedent rather than invent a third pattern — and PR #94's text explicitly asks for that.

## MVP

The status-strip half of the original MVP has shipped as its own message kind. What remains is the general channel: give `simulation/delta` a **sender**, since its schema already exists and already enforces `tick > baseTick`, and carry the seven unreachable projections over it rather than adding a third bespoke message kind.

## The failure mode to design against

A per-tick firehose that serialises every projection every tick and eats the frame budget — precisely the long-task problem the worker split exists to prevent. Mitigations, all of which the repo already has opinions about:

- Send on a **cadence** (the research suggested ~500 ms of simulated time, or on change), never per tick. The tick loop wakes every 15 ms and the loop already carries snapshots.
- **Stamp every payload with the tick it describes**, so a projection cannot silently drift out of sync with the state it claims to report. PR #94 does this for the clock, and `deltaMessageSchema` already requires both `baseTick` and `tick`.
- Honour `docs/HUD_PROJECTIONS.md` contract 5 (paging) rather than sending unbounded lists.
- Budget and measure it. `AGENTS.md` requires performance evidence for performance-sensitive systems, and a boundary that also carries session snapshots qualifies.

## Sequencing note

Its *value* partly depends on #89 — while no build order can complete and no prisoner arrives, the counts are honestly zero and making them live changes little on screen. But its *cost* does not depend on #89 at all, and every explanation and onboarding feature needs it, so there is no reason to wait. Build it in parallel with the procurement work.

Not in scope: what to *do* with the data. The explanation panel, blocked-intent reporting and onboarding predicates are separate issues that consume this channel.

Refs #89, #94, #157. Governed by ADR 0003 and ADR 0006; `docs/HUD_PROJECTIONS.md` gaps.

items.title: [Incidents] Hiring one guard makes the incident system mathematically unreachable, and the only prison that riots has no guards to respond — `IncidentResponseSystem` has never executed in a playable prison
items.body:
## Context

Found by a long-run playthrough audit that drove the real simulation for 60,000 ticks per
configuration. **The arithmetic below I re-verified myself against the source before filing.**

`DEFAULT_SECTOR_RISK_POLICY` (`src/simulation/incidents/sector-risk.ts:35-38`):

```ts
needsPressureWeight: 0.5,
staffingShortfallWeight: 0.3,
contrabandPressureWeight: 0.2,
hotThreshold: 0.6,
```

`contrabandPressure` reads `IntelligenceLedger`, and **nothing in `src/` ever writes to it**, so
that term is structurally 0. The score is therefore capped at
`0.5·needsPressure + 0.3·staffingShortfall`.

The derived default sector requires **one** guard (`security/default-sector.ts`). Hire one and
`staffingShortfall` becomes 0, leaving a ceiling of **0.5 — below the 0.6 threshold at any
level of misery whatsoever.**

Measured, guard-count sweep on the one prison that can generate needs pressure, 60,000 ticks
each, 16 prisoners driven to safety 0:

| guards | assigned | max risk score | incidents | resolved | lapsed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | **0.80** | **69** | 0 | 68 |
| 1 | 1 | **0.50** | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | 1 | 0.50 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 4 | 1 | 0.50 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

## And in an ordinary prison the score never even approaches it

`resolveSectorOccupants` (`new-session.ts:591-605`) counts only prisoners standing **exactly on
the sector's single post tile**. Once intake completes, every prisoner teleports to a room
anchor. Measured `occupantsAtPostTileMax: 0`, so needs pressure is **0 by construction in any
prison that houses anybody**: max score 0.0078 with four guards, 0.308 with zero, over 60,000
ticks.

So the only configuration that riots is the one where nobody was ever housed — a zoned cell
with no bed, prisoners stalled at `accommodation-assignment` on the arrival tile, which *is*
the post tile. First riot at tick 15,501; 69 riots over 60,000 ticks, severities 6–8, 16
participants each. **68 lapsed, 1 active, 0 resolved** — because the only configuration that
triggers a riot is the one with no guards to respond to it.

**`IncidentResponseSystem`'s entire `notified → responding → resolved` pipeline — the lockdown,
`respondersDispatched`, `incidentsResolved`, `injuredEntityIds` — has never executed in any
prison a player can build.** `respondersDispatched: 0` in every run.

## What else in the security tier never fires

- **Three of four authored incident types have no producer.** `IncidentTriggerSystem` opens only
  `'riot'` (`trigger-system.ts:95`) and `'gang-retaliation'` (`:120`), and the latter needs
  `GangRegistry` entries nothing in `src/` writes. Measured: 69/69 incidents were `riot`;
  `retaliationsTriggered: 0`, `gangGrudges: 0`, `tunnels: 0`. `assault` and `escape-attempt`
  have **no producer anywhere**.
- **All five contraband types.** Nothing calls `ContrabandRegistry.introduce` outside its own
  module and the tests. After 50,000 ticks in a working prison: `contrabandItems: 0`,
  `confiscations: 0`, `searchMetrics` all zero. `SearchSystem` runs 2,000 times per 20,000 ticks
  over an empty queue, and `ReleaseGuardAssignment` therefore has nothing it can ever release.
- **`PatrolSystem`** ran 2,000 times over 50,000 ticks reporting
  `{loopsCompletedOnTime: 0, loopsCompletedLate: 0, loopsMissed: 0}` — the derived default
  sector has no patrol route, by design (`default-sector.ts:194`).
- **The riot regime never applies.** `applyRiotRegimeOverride` (`riot-regime.ts:35`) is called
  only from `tests/unit/incident-escape-riot.test.ts`. A riot changes no prisoner's timetable —
  and see #440 for why it could not help if it did.
- **Seven of eight staff roles are interchangeable, and the wrong one gets the post.**
  `HireStaff` accepted all eight roles with zero refusals and put all eight on `GuardRoster`;
  `DeploymentSystem` filled the sector's one post with **entity 0, `staff-role.administrator`,
  phase `on-post`**. A warden, a nurse and a cook are all riot police. The other seven hires are
  paid for and stand idle for ever, because the prison requires exactly one guard however large
  it is.

## In scope

- Decide whether the threshold, the weights, or the required-guard count is what is wrong. It
  cannot be none of them: as it stands, one hire disables the mechanic.
- **`resolveSectorOccupants` counting only the post tile is the more fundamental half** — it
  makes needs pressure structurally unreachable in every playable prison, independently of the
  threshold. Decide what a sector's occupants are.
- Whether a sector's `requiredGuardCount` should scale with population.
- The decision belongs in an ADR; `CLAUDE.md` forbids taking it inside implementation code.

## Out of scope

- Authoring the missing incident producers (`assault`, `escape-attempt`) and the contraband
  introduction path — each deserves its own issue once this one establishes whether the trigger
  can fire at all.
- Consequences for the prisoner involved — that is #80.
- The action-category gap (#440) and the release loop (#441).
- `supabase/migrations/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A furnished prison with guards on the payroll can reach `hotThreshold` under sustained
      neglect — shown by a run with the score over time, not by arithmetic.
- [ ] `IncidentResponseSystem` reaches `resolved` at least once in a run, with
      `respondersDispatched > 0` and the lockdown lifting.
- [ ] The guard-count sweep is re-run and reported: the score must not collapse below the
      threshold at the first hire.
- [ ] Determinism unchanged: two runs from one seed byte-identical, shown not asserted.
- [ ] `pnpm verify` green.

## Required verification

- **A green suite is not a guarded suite**: mutate the risk weights or the occupancy resolution
  and watch a named test go red, then restore. Both outputs in the commit message.
- Re-run the 0/1/2/4-guard sweep and report all four rows. The measurement above is one seed and
  one sector — **that is this issue's weakest evidence**; the arithmetic
  (`0.5 + 0.2·0 < 0.6`) is what makes it certain, not the sweep.
- One caveat the audit flagged and a fix must not rely on: `runtime.securitySchedules` is a live
  array, so a future feature registering a second sector with a larger `requiredGuardCount`
  could hold `staffingShortfall ≥ 0.667` and reach the threshold. Nothing in `src/` does that
  today.

## Performance constraints

`security.deployment` already costs 152 µs per call to place one guard on one post, measured at
200 prisoners. If occupancy resolution becomes a spatial query, state its cost.

## Documentation impact

`docs/PRISONER_OPERATIONS.md` and any security document describing the incident lifecycle;
`default-sector.ts` and `riot-regime.ts` header comments, which describe behaviour that cannot
happen; new ADR.

items.title: Branch triage after v0.0.37: 92 unmerged branches
items.body:
Triage of every remote branch not merged into `main`, against `main` = `d2596ad` (`chore(release): v0.0.37`). Read-only: nothing was pushed, deleted, committed, merged, or opened as a PR.

## First, the count is wrong — and that matters

The clone this triage started in was **shallow** (`.git/shallow` present; `git rev-list --count origin/main` reported 133 instead of 602). `git branch -r --no-merged` cannot see past a graft boundary, so it reports as "unmerged" every branch whose merge base was cut off. That is the entire origin of the number 92.

After `git fetch --unshallow`:

| | count |
|---|---|
| Remote branches total | 124 |
| Strict ancestors of `origin/main` | 102 |
| **Genuinely not merged** | **22** |

**70 of the 92 are already fully merged.** Each was checked individually with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> origin/main`; all 70 returned true. They can be deleted with the 31 already tracked in #291, with no further review — that issue's set is 31 of 101, not 31 of 31.

Anyone else running this triage should `git fetch --unshallow` first, or they will re-derive the same false 92.

## Counts per category

Over the 22 genuinely unmerged branches:

| Category | Count |
|---|---|
| **SUPERSEDED** | **22** |
| **LIVE** | **0** |
| **CONFLICTED-STALE** | **0** |
| **EMPTY** | **0** |
| **UNKNOWN** | **0** |

Plus **70 MERGED** outside that set (shallow-clone false positives, above).

## LIVE (0)

**There are none.** Every one of the 22 is a pre-squash-merge snapshot of work that reached `main` through a squash-merged PR — squash merge is exactly why the branch tips are not in `main`'s ancestry even though the content is — or, in one case, a proposal `main` rejected in writing.

This is a real finding rather than a shrug: it means the 22 can be deleted, not finished.

## How "superseded" was established

Branch names and commit subjects were not trusted. For each branch:

1. `git diff --name-only origin/main...<branch>` for the files it touches.
2. On those files only, **two-dot** `git diff origin/main..<branch>` — branch against `main`'s actual tip. Lines the branch would *add* to `main` are candidate unlanded value; lines it would *remove* are `main` having moved on.
3. Every exported symbol, type, and test title the branch introduces, extracted from the diff and grepped against a materialised checkout of `origin/main`.
4. Every residual line from steps 2–3 read by hand.
5. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <branch>` for merge cleanliness — no worktree created, no merge performed.

Below, **code+** is the count of real code lines (in `src/ tests/ tooling/ supabase/ scripts/`, comment- and brace-only lines dropped) the branch would add to `main`. **code+ = 0 means the branch holds no code `main` lacks.**

## SUPERSEDED (22)

### Byte-identical to `main` on every file they touch (7)

`+0 / -0` against `main`'s tip. Nothing to salvage, nothing to lose.

| Branch | Ahead | Merges clean | Landed as |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claude/adr-room-capacity` | 1 | yes | `a41ec30` (#289) — ADR 0023 identical, all 716 lines |
| `claude/doc-path-citation-gate` | 1 | yes | `ea98c35` (#268) — `documentation-links-contract.test.ts` identical |
| `claude/rng-derivation-vector` | 1 | yes | `11662bc` (#270) — golden-vector test and all five literals present |
| `claude/rpc-status-mapping` | 2 | yes | `7977494` (#272) — `supabase-client.ts` and its test identical |
| `claude/save-import` | 2 | yes | `d73274c` (#290) — `main` has `parseImportedSave`, `describeImportResult`, `SaveImportResult` and every `statusImport*` key; no branch symbol or locale key missing |
| `claude/slow-test-timing` | 1 | yes | `948f2a4` (#271) — both test files identical |
| `claude/wooden-door-geometry` | 1 | yes | `95cc881` (#266) — `docs/NAVIGATION.md` and `construction/definition.ts` identical |

### Absorbed, with `main` strictly ahead (14)

The substance is in `main`; the branch additionally holds an *older* revision of the same prose or tests, so the two-dot diff is not empty. Every residue was read: it is stale text `main` has since corrected. Merging any of these would **regress** `main`.

| Branch | Ahead | +/− vs main | code+ | Merges clean | Landed as |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claude/adr-corpus-corrections` | 1 | +20 / −109 | 0 | no | `16aa2e2` (#284) |
| `claude/adr-room-zoning-surface` | 2 | +17 / −17 | 0 | no | `ea2aedb` (#286) |
| `claude/challenge-verification-guards` | 2 | +8 / −23 | 0 | no | `ac9f6d3` (#273) |
| `claude/message-kind-reachability` | 2 | +3 / −3 | 0 | no | `1229c09` (#281) |
| `claude/mutation-survivors` | 2 | +49 / −1056 | 3 | no | `f1a661c` (#275) |
| `claude/needs-decay-fixed-point` | 2 | +43 / −353 | 0 | yes | `d701e1b` (#276) |
| `claude/purchase-refusal-seam` | 8 | +81 / −719 | 7 | no | `c2b5a28` (#282) + `e5d54ed` (#283) |
| `claude/purchase-stepper` | 4 | +77 / −1141 | 8 | no | `c2b5a28` (#282) |
| `claude/reachable-undo` | 2 | +92 / −882 | 17 | no | `060a796` (#279) |
| `claude/render-actors` | 1 | +13 / −196 | 3 | yes | `50e7453` (#267) |
| `claude/report-refusals` | 4 | +6 / −526 | 3 | no | `e5d54ed` (#283) |
| `claude/sql-tier-audit` | 2 | +5 / −31 | 0 | yes | `ced65b2` (#277) |
| `claude/zone-room-registers` | 3 | +104 / −379 | 19 | no | `041a379` (#269) |
| `claude/lockstate-environment-setup-gmi1pd` | 1 | +51 / −105 | 0 | no | `95a6f2e` (#138) — resolved the *opposite* way, see below |

Spot evidence for the non-zero `code+` rows, since those are the only ones where "superseded" is not self-evident:

- **`claude/reachable-undo`** — two of its test titles do not resolve in `main`, and both times `main` holds the successor: `it('measures three produced and three unproduced, which is the state #89 is really about')` is now `it('measures four produced and two unproduced, which is where #89 left the command surface')`, and `'names an outcome for each command, and four different ones'` is now `'... and five different ones'` (`main` gained the purchase refusal). The other 17 lines are pre-#282 `PurchaseMaterials` "still unreachable" annotations.
- **`claude/zone-room-registers`** — `src/simulation/prisoners/room-instance-registry.ts` is identical to `main`; all 33 introduced symbols/test titles resolve. The 19 lines are pre-#283 comments ("A refusal has nowhere to go", "The outcome is deliberately dropped here") that `main` deleted when the refusal route was actually built.
- **`claude/purchase-stepper` / `claude/report-refusals` / `claude/purchase-refusal-seam`** — `purchase-refusal-seam` is the other two merged plus one extra commit, `test(browser): a refused purchase produces exactly one message`. That commit is in `main` too: `tests/browser/app-shell.spec.ts` carries claim 13 verbatim ("**A refused purchase produces exactly one player-visible message.**") and both tests. The branch header says "Thirteen claims"; `main` says "Fourteen". The remaining residue is an older `ui-save-panel-status.test.ts` key list `['create','save','load','delete','export']` — `main`'s has `'import'` as well, because #290 landed after.
- **`claude/mutation-survivors`** — `tooling/build-source-art-catalog.mjs`, `tooling/source-art-lfs-guard.mjs`/`.d.mts` and `src/services/telemetry/redaction.ts` are identical to `main`; all 20 introduced symbols/test titles resolve. The 3 lines are an older Playwright locator where `main` is 840 lines ahead.
- **`claude/render-actors`** — `actors-from-snapshot.ts`, `simulation-snapshot-feed.ts` and `entity-store.ts` are all identical to `main`. The 3 lines are older `src/main.ts` wiring.
- **`claude/lockstate-environment-setup-gmi1pd`** — the one branch `main` resolved the **opposite** way rather than by landing it. The branch makes `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` *run* `scripts/provision-git-lfs.sh` and `scripts/provision-playwright-browsers.sh`. `main` (`95a6f2e`, #138) deliberately runs neither and says so in the hook: "CI runs scripts/provision-git-lfs.sh … and scripts/provision-playwright-browsers.sh …; **this hook runs neither**, because `git lfs pull` is metered bandwidth and the browsers are a ~280 MiB download" — it probes and reports instead. Both scripts exist on `main`. Reinstating auto-provisioning would be a new decision, not a merge.

### Superseded by an explicit written rejection (1)

`claude/construction-materials-supply` — 3 commits ahead, **420 behind**, 24 files, `+953 / −1433`, **code+ 382**, conflicts in 8 files.

This is the **only branch in the entire set holding substantial code `main` does not have**: `src/content/scenario-catalog.ts`, `src/simulation/runtime/apply-scenario.ts`, `docs/adr/0018-construction-material-supply.md`, `tests/integration/construction-material-loop.test.ts`, `tests/unit/scenario-starting-stock.test.ts` — `applyScenario`, `STARTER_SCENARIO`, `scenarioStartingStockSchema` and friends, none of which appear anywhere in `main`.

It is still superseded, and the repository says so in its own words. `docs/adr/README.md` on `main`, section "0018, and why it is free again":

> It was reserved by PR #91, which added `docs/adr/0018-construction-material-supply.md` and was held by an explicit owner decision. That PR has been **closed as superseded by #249** — its `startingStock` proposal was replaced by a money opening balance, which is ADR 0017 decision 1 — so this table releases the number.

The supply route itself did land, by the other design: `ContainerMaterialsProvider` is wired into the real runtime at `src/simulation/runtime/new-session.ts:230`, with `src/simulation/construction/materials-provider.ts` and `src/simulation/operations/inventory.ts` on `main`.

Conflicts include `src/simulation/construction/{definition,materials-provider,system}.ts` and `src/simulation/worker/state-machine.ts`, so reviving it would be a rewrite, not a merge. **This is the only branch worth a human glance before deletion**, and only to confirm the #91-closed-by-#249 decision still stands.

## CONFLICTED-STALE (0)

None *as a residual-value category*. Fourteen of the 22 do fail `git merge-tree --write-tree` against `main`, but in every case the conflict is `main` having moved past an already-landed copy of the same change — not unlanded work that drifted.

## EMPTY (0)

No branch is empty in the "nothing but a version bump or a merge commit" sense. The seven byte-identical branches above are the closest thing, and they are filed as SUPERSEDED because their content is provably *in* `main` rather than absent from both.

## UNKNOWN (0)

Nothing was left undetermined. Every classification rests on mechanical evidence — `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, blob comparison, symbol and test-title resolution against a materialised `origin/main` tree — plus hand-reading of every residual line.

## `origin/archive/*`

One branch, and it happens to be a strict ancestor of `origin/main`:

Existence and date only, per scope. No triage performed and none needed.

## The 70 already-merged branches (shallow-clone false positives)

All verified strict ancestors of `origin/main`. Dates run 2026-08-23 to 2026-08-24.

items.title: [Prisoners] Under contention the same prisoners lose the same room for ever: order the contended scan by need urgency (ADR 0041 decision 2, ADR 0029 decision 5's fairness half)
items.body:
## Context

ADR 0041 decision 2, recorded verbatim in the ADR:

> **Ordering the contended scan by need urgency is the tracked successor, not part of
> this decision.** It is recorded here as the answer to ADR 0029 decision 5's fairness
> half and is deliberately not taken now.

ADR 0041 fixed the **base case**: a prisoner whose best action cannot resolve a target
now falls back to the next-best legal action in the same cycle, so a prison with no
canteen feeds its prisoners and `action.eat-in-cell` became reachable content for the
first time. What it explicitly did **not** fix is fairness, and the ADR's own
Consequences say so: *"Under contention the losers eat a worse meal instead of
nothing. The unfairness ADR 0029 decision 5 accepted is unchanged, and stays open
as B."*

**The mechanism, as measured.** Room use is claimed in a single ascending scan over
the population, and each claim is visible to the next prisoner in the same walk. So
the losing set is decided by index order and, because the winners' needs are refilled
and the losers' are not, **the losing set never reopens** — the ADR calls this
incumbency and names it the measured mechanism. ADR 0029's amendment run: 24
prisoners, 24,000 ticks, a canteen seating six; eighteen prisoners ate nothing.

ADR 0029 decision 5 accepted this on two grounds, both since measured false: that a
fix is ADR 0020's per-tick ordering territory, and that *"it is also not yet
observable"*. Its revisit condition — a need readout — **cannot fire on its own
terms**, because no HUD surface requests the projection that carries need levels.

ADR 0041 deferred B **"on cost and scope, not on merit"**, and named the three things
that have to be settled to take it.

## In scope

Take alternative B, or argue a better one down from the same evidence. The ADR's
stated obstacles are the work:

- **Which need decides urgency**, when a prisoner is hungry and filthy at once. ADR
  0041 says explicitly that it *"forces a question this document should not answer
  alone"*. Answer it, with an argument, in an ADR — not inside implementation code
  (`CLAUDE.md`).
- **A second iteration order over the population at `O(N log N)` per cycle.** Measure
  it against the current per-tick cost rather than asserting it is affordable; #288
  established that navigation, not system count, is where the tick cost actually is,
  so measure against that baseline.
- **Determinism.** A new ordering over the population is exactly what ADR 0020 governs
  and what ADR 0029 decision 7's four commitments constrain. A tie in urgency must
  break by something total and reproducible; no RNG, no `Map` insertion accident, no
  wall-clock.

Consider the alternatives ADR 0041 rejected before re-deriving them: **C** (a
round-robin cursor per room instance — collides with ADR 0029 decision 6's argument
for keeping use claims out of the save) and **D** (a reservation at selection with an
expiry — fixes incumbency but not index order, and is the heaviest).

Also in scope, because it is the same walk: ADR 0029 decision 7 **commitment 4** — *a
refused claim mutates nothing* — is currently held in the code but **unguarded**, and
ADR 0041's amendment says a mutation violating it left the whole suite green. The
branch is unreachable in today's single-threaded ascending scan; a reordered or
parallel scan is precisely what would make it reachable. If this issue changes that
scan, the commitment must gain a guard in the same change.

## Out of scope

- Any change to what a need *does*. `hunger` still has no downstream consumer — only
  `safety` has one (`new-session.ts:616` → `IncidentTriggerSystem`). Consequences for a
  starving prisoner are #80's and #31's territory, not this issue's.
- The need readout itself (see Dependencies).
- Any save-schema change. If urgency ordering needs persisted state, that is ADR 0029
  decision 6's argument to reopen, and #288 prices a V-bump — stop and raise it.
- `supabase/migrations/`.

## Dependencies

- **ADR 0041** (decision 2 is this issue), **ADR 0029** (decisions 5, 6 and 7), **ADR
  0020** (deterministic kernel — ordering).
- **The need readout.** ADR 0041 states B *"is the right decision to take when a need
  readout ships, because that is when the unfairness becomes visible to a player."*
  No HUD surface requests the need projection today; #104 is where that channel's
  unreached projections live. **This issue does not have to wait for it** — the
  unfairness is real without a readout — but taking it blind means nobody can see the
  fix work, so land or borrow a readout as part of the verification.
- A new ADR for the urgency question. **Ask for the number rather than claiming one**
  (`docs/adr/README.md` records the next free number; ADR numbers are assigned
  centrally, and 0038 was drafted twice in parallel by two agents once already).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An ADR records which need decides urgency and why, with its Status stating what
      was approved and by whom.
- [ ] In a run with more prisoners than canteen seats, **the losing set changes over
      time**: assert that a named prisoner who lost one meal cycle wins a later one.
      Not a variance statistic, not a count — a named entity's own history.
- [ ] Two runs from the same seed produce byte-identical fingerprints, and the
      fingerprint test's expected value is updated in the same commit that moves it,
      with the reason in the message.
- [ ] Measured per-cycle cost at `DEFAULT_PRISONER_CAPACITY`-scale population, stated
      as a number against the pre-change baseline.
- [ ] ADR 0029 decision 7 commitment 4 has a guard that goes red when the
      mutates-nothing branch is broken — or a written statement that this change did
      not make it reachable, with the reachability argument.
- [ ] ADR 0029 decision 5's Status is amended to point at the decision that closed
      it, and ADR 0041 decision 2 is marked taken.
- [ ] `pnpm verify` green.

## Required verification

- **A green suite is not a guarded suite**: mutate the urgency comparator and watch a
  named test go red, then restore it and watch it go green. Both outputs in the commit
  message.
- The fairness assertion must not be self-fulfilling (#375): do not derive the
  expected winner from the same ordering function under test, and do not compare one
  simulated run against another simulated run as the whole of the claim.
- Re-run ADR 0029's amendment scenario (24 prisoners, 24,000 ticks, canteen seating
  six) and report the per-prisoner meal counts before and after, since that
  measurement is what made this a decision rather than an opinion.

## Performance constraints

Per-cycle, population-wide. State the added cost at 24, 500 and 5,000 prisoners
against the measured pre-change tick cost. #288's finding stands: navigation dominates
the tick, so an `O(N log N)` pass may be free — but it must be shown to be, not
assumed.

## Documentation impact

New ADR (urgency); ADR 0029 (decision 5 closed, decision 7 commitment 4 if guarded);
ADR 0041 (decision 2 taken); `docs/SIMULATION.md` action selection; `docs/TESTING.md`
if the fingerprint's meaning changes.

items.title: [Continuation prompt] START HERE after the 2026-08-27 session — one blocker, four product decisions, and the traps that cost this session hours
items.body:
You are taking over Lockstate. Read `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/AGENT_WORKFLOW.md` first — they are the contract, not background reading. This issue is what the previous session knew that those documents do not say.

---

## Where things stand

**Branch of record: `claude/lockstate-agents-prompt-tlyafw`, 112 commits ahead of `main`, open as [#430](https://github.com/matmaxalez/lockstate/pull/430).** Nothing is uncommitted and nothing is unpushed.

Green on that head: `verify` (259 files / 2,879 tests), `assets`, `verify:sql` (321 assertions), `verify:benchmark` (11 deterministic scenarios). **Red: `browser`.**

### The one blocker, and read this before touching it

`browser` failed twice on this branch, on **different tests in different files**, both 60-second page-load timeouts inside setup helpers that most of the suite also uses (`openApp`'s `waitForSelector('#game-root canvas')`; a `beforeEach`'s `waitForFunction('lockstateUiHarness' in window)`). 203 tests passed in each of those runs, and a **fully green 204/204 run sits between the two failures** — on a head that already contains the render-feed change, which is the only commit with a plausible mechanism for slowing first paint.

The re-run allowance is **spent**. Do not re-run again to see what happens.

The previous session could not root-cause it and said so in a PR comment rather than hand-waving. **You cannot reproduce it in the dev container**: `public/assets/**` is Git LFS pointer text there, so `pnpm test:browser` fails at the same place by design. That is the documented baseline, not a regression.

Three things would settle it, cheapest first: the `error-context.md` Playwright wrote beside each failure (it captures page state at the timeout); whether the two runners differ (they do — `-2` and `-3`, which **weakens** the "busy machine" reading rather than supporting it, and the previous session recorded that against its own argument); and a `browser` run on a quiet host. **Start there. Do not start by editing test code.**

---

## What is decided and what is not

**Decided this session, by the owner's standing delegation to decide autonomously** — ADRs 0038 through 0044. Each Status records that the approval is of the judgement delegated and **not of the text**, and that a disagreeing reader should treat it as open. That is not boilerplate: if you disagree with one, say so and re-open it rather than working around it.

**Open, and genuinely the owner's — do not decide these yourself:**

1. **Does cloud save ship?** Everything else is ready: the server half is 23 migrations and 321 pgTAP assertions run on every CI run, the client is written, both deploy secrets are already required "ahead of the client that will read them". Missing is an account UX (#34) and the decision. ADR 0044 has the full argument.
2. **Does Lockstate collect telemetry?** A "no" supersedes ADR 0010 and makes 771 lines deletable in one commit. Note what makes this urgent rather than tidy: `grep` the built bundle and you find *"Help improve Lockstate"*, *"5 extra prison slots"* and `telemetry.consent.title` shipping to players, and **zero** references to the code behind any of them.
3. **Is `roomPerimeterEnclosure` meant to stay advisory?** It refuses nothing today — `zone` accepts an open room and only the Rooms panel reads the result. The answer decides whether [#445](https://github.com/matmaxalez/lockstate/issues/445)'s three enclosure survivors cost a wrong *sentence* or a wrong *prison*, and therefore whether they outrank the pathfinding-fairness survivor.
4. **The product loop.** #440–#443 are four measured findings from a long-run playthrough nobody had ever run. They are not bugs to fix one at a time; together they say the simulation is a correct, deterministic, fast needs-and-rooms loop **with no consequences attached to it**, in a prison that cannot grow, cannot lose money, cannot release anybody, and — once one guard is hired — cannot have anything go wrong.

---

## Where to spend effort, and why

**[#445](https://github.com/matmaxalez/lockstate/issues/445) first.** A 47-mutation sweep put `src/simulation/rooms/` at a **38% kill rate** holding 5 of 11 survivors, while kernel, economy, worker and persistence are 19 for 19. It names three survivors *and writes the test that kills each*, including why each test must be shaped the way it is (a non-square rectangle, so one axis cannot mask the other; an id that sorts *against* the property under test, so deleting the clause fails too and not only reversing it; a rating above the early-exit floor, or the case is vacuous). That is the highest value-per-hour work available.

**Then [#444](https://github.com/matmaxalez/lockstate/issues/444)**, which contains the sharpest single finding of the session: `fault-code-reachability-contract` asserts *"Empty, and that is the assertion"* — and passes, because `'shutting-down'` appears three times **inside its own producing surface**, every time as a worker state and never as a fault. Renaming the state (a pure refactor) turns the gate red instantly.

**Then the product decisions above.** #440–#443 need an owner's ruling before code.

Everything else is enumerated in #431–#443.

---

## The five traps that cost the previous session real time

**1. `isolation: worktree` branches agents off `main`, not off the branch of record.** It caught **every single agent** — some 70+ commits stale. Two of them measured entire censuses against the wrong tree before noticing. Put this in every agent brief, verbatim:

```
git fetch origin claude/lockstate-agents-prompt-tlyafw
git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/claude/lockstate-agents-prompt-tlyafw HEAD && echo OK || echo STALE
```

and if STALE with no local commits, `git reset --hard <branch head>`.

**2. Never mutation-test in the shared checkout.** Concurrent agents mutate `src/` in flight. One run was contaminated into 37 unrelated failures; worse, a *contaminated* run once reported a **survivor as KILLED, by a test in an unrelated file**. `git archive HEAD | tar -x` into a scratch mirror costs 8 MB and one command.

**3. Whole-suite runs are not reproducible under load.** Identical clean trees gave 9, 5 and 5 failures, every one a `Test timed out in 5000ms`, every named file green in isolation. **Attribute mutation results file by file, never by counting failures.** A mutation that killed only a flaky file reads as a survivor.

**4. A sha read out of an agent's own worktree is dead the moment you cherry-pick it.** `tests/foundation/documentation-commit-citation-contract.test.ts` now fails the build on a fabricated *or unpublished* sha. Check both: `git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}` **and** `git branch -r --contains <sha>`.

**5. `file:line` citations rot within hours in files under active edit.** This session re-anchored ten ADRs and then watched two of the replacements drift again the same morning. Cite by **symbol name and quotation**. And note the finding that contradicts the obvious lesson: ADR 0038 pins its citations to a named sha, and two of three sampled anchors had drifted anyway — **pinning does not stop rot, it makes rot diagnosable.**

---

## The rules that are load-bearing, not decoration

- **"A green suite is not a guarded suite."** No guard counts until you mutate the production code, watch it go red, restore, and watch it go green — with both outputs in the commit message. This session found three whole-suite survivors that a green run had been hiding, and one gate that passed on a name collision inside itself.
- **Never report a result you did not obtain.** This repository has a documented history of confident false findings and two fabricated commit shas, one of them shipped.
- **Reproduce a delegated finding before acting on it.** It paid off repeatedly here: a proposed fix would have deleted the *live* half of a key family and adopted a pattern an Accepted ADR rejects by name; another "sometimes" turned out to be "always"; a third finding was worse than reported by six commits.
- **`docs/research/` is read-only history.** Its README says it: *"when the code moves on, a record here does not become wrong, it becomes older."* The test for whether a stale count is a defect is not "is it current" but **"does the document claim to be"**.
- **A count in prose rots**, and fastest where the thing counted is under active work. ADR 0044 landed with a correct number and was overtaken **within the hour**. Write the command that derives it, or write a subject instead of a tally.

## Hard constraints

Do **not** touch `supabase/migrations/` — a migration that has been applied is history; propose new migration content instead. Do **not** run, re-run or dispatch a hosted workflow. Do **not** infer the Supabase project ref from CI metadata — that is the owner's. Never `git add -A`. No scratch files under `tests/`. Push only to the designated branch. **Do not merge or open a pull request without the owner asking.**

---

## One thing worth carrying forward

The best work this session produced came from agents **refusing** the instruction they were given and saying why, with evidence. Three did it and all three were right. If a brief tells you to do something the code contradicts, the brief is what is wrong.

items.title: [Tests] A contract test titled "with a content hash" never hashes anything, plus three more tests that cannot fail or point at files that do not exist
items.body:
Split from **#124 item 6**. Re-verified against current `main`.

This is the same class as #113 (nine surviving `ConstructionSystem` mutations) and the `camera-coordinates` round-trip that #115 turned out to rest on: a green assertion that cannot go red. Filed separately from #113 because none of these is in `ConstructionSystem` and each is independently fixable.

---

## 1. `art-pipeline-contract.test.ts` — the title claims content hashing; the file imports no hashing function

**VERIFIED.** The test is titled:

> `publishes every owner-supplied object sheet with a content hash and attribution`

and its body is:

```ts
for (const entry of catalog.entries) {
  expect(entry.sha256).toMatch(/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/);
  expect(entry.sourceAttribution.license).toBe('owner-supplied, project-internal');
  await access(resolve(root, 'public/game-content', entry.image));
}
```

It asserts that the field **looks like** a sha256, that a license string matches, and that a file **exists** at the declared path. It never reads the image bytes and never recomputes the digest — `grep` for `createHash` in that file returns **nothing**; its only `node:fs/promises` imports are `access` and `readFile`, and `readFile` is used exclusively on JSON.

So `source-art.v1.json` could declare **any** well-formed hash for **any** image — or the same hash for all 23 — and this test passes. The one thing a content hash is for, detecting that the bytes changed, is unchecked.

**The fix is four lines:** read the image, `createHash('sha256')`, compare to `entry.sha256`. That turns the title into a true statement.

**Note the interaction with git-lfs, which makes this worth doing carefully:** in an environment without `git-lfs`, those PNGs are 131-byte pointer files, so a real digest check would fail for the *right* reason but look like a broken test — the same trap that makes `app-shell.spec.ts`'s atlas decode the documented baseline failure. The fix should therefore **detect a pointer file and say so explicitly**, exactly as `tooling/validate-runtime-atlas.mjs` already does, rather than reporting a hash mismatch. That precedent exists and should be followed.

## 2. `prisoners-regime.test.ts` — samples 18 of 2,400 ticks and asserts only that nothing threw

**VERIFIED.** It walks the day with a stride of 137, giving 18 samples out of `DAY_LENGTH_TICKS` = 2,400, and asserts no throw. It never asserts that every tick maps to a block, never asserts "exactly once", never inspects the returned block.

Also largely **redundant**: the real gate is the module-load validator, which runs regardless.

The honest options are to make it a real test (assert full coverage of the day, and that block boundaries are where the definition says) or to delete it and say the validator is the gate. **Sampling 0.75% of the domain and asserting absence of a throw is the one option that should not stay**, because it reads as coverage.

## 3. A test points at a spec file that has never existed

**VERIFIED.** `tests/unit/ui-async-action-gate.test.ts` directs the reader to `tests/browser/save-panel-concurrency.spec.ts`. That file **does not exist** — `ls tests/browser/` has no such entry.

The coverage itself **does** exist, in `ui-shell.spec.ts`. So this is a stale filename, not a hole — but it is the only thing telling a reader where the browser-layer half of this contract lives, and it sends them nowhere.

**Same defect, different file:** `src/content/room-catalog.ts` names `room-catalog-adapter.ts`, which has **never existed** in the repository's history. The conversion is done by `roomDefinitionFromCatalog`.

Both are one-line fixes, and both are the doc-truth defect class this repository spends the most effort on — a confident pointer to a file that is not there.

## 4. The determinism flake, which matters because of *how* it fails

**VERIFIED and reproduced repeatedly during this session** — it fired once in a run with four agents loading the CPU and passed immediately on re-run.

`tests/unit/prisoners-operations-scenario.test.ts` → *"an identical seed and scenario produce an identical fingerprint"* needs roughly **6 s** under CPU load, against `vitest.config.ts`'s `testTimeout: 5_000`. It passes in isolation and **fails on `main` too**, so no branch causes it.

**Why it is worth fixing rather than tolerating:** a timeout inside a determinism test is reported as *"an identical seed and scenario produce an identical fingerprint" failed* — which in this repository is **the most alarming possible false positive.** Determinism is an ADR 0009 product guarantee, and every handover document has to spend a paragraph telling the next session that this particular determinism failure is not a determinism failure. That paragraph has now been written at least three times.

Three fixes, and the choice matters:
- **Raise the timeout for that test only.** Cheapest, keeps the coverage, but leaves a slow test that will creep back up.
- **Split it**, so the fingerprint comparison is its own fast test and the expensive scenario setup is shared or reduced. Best outcome, most work.
- **Make it cheaper** (fewer ticks, smaller scenario) — but the run length may be load-bearing for what it proves, so this needs checking rather than assuming.

**Do not** mark it `.skip`. A skipped determinism test is worse than a flaky one, and CI's `browser` job already has a guard against skipping its way to green precisely because that was judged the worse failure.

---

## What ties these together

Each is a test whose *title* or *pointer* promises more than its body delivers. That is not a coverage gap — a coverage gap is visible. It is a green check that a reader reasonably counts as covering something, which is why #113 and #115 both cost a live defect before anyone looked.

The cheapest general defence is the one already used elsewhere here: **when adding a test, name a one-line mutation to the code it covers and run it.** #115's round-trip test and #113's nine survivors would both have been caught the first time by that one habit.

items.title: The alerts list has an `info` severity that nothing has ever produced — the prison can only report what went wrong
items.body:
This is a synthesis, not a new defect. Findings from tonight's playtests (#503, #506, and ADR 0067's own unbuilt list) turn out to share one cause, and naming it makes several pending decisions cheaper to take together than separately.

## The finding

`HudAlertViewModel` (`src/ui/hud/view-model.ts:146`) is **generic**: an id, a message key, optional parameters, and a severity. Its severity type is

```ts
export type HudSeverity = 'info' | 'warning' | 'danger';   // view-model.ts:144
```

The alerts list will happily render a neutral row. **Nothing has ever given it one.**

The restriction is not in the view model — it is entirely in the producer. `src/ui/simulation-alerts.ts` builds alerts from exactly two closed unions, `RefusalReason` and `ProtocolFaultCode`, and assigns only:

- `severity: 'warning'` for every refusal (`:220`)
- `severity: recoverable ? 'warning' : 'danger'` for protocol faults (`:250`)

**`'info'` is assigned nowhere in that file.** (Guarding against a grep trap: `'info'` does appear elsewhere in `src/ui/**`, but those are `BadgeTone` — `src/ui/primitives/status-badge.ts:11` — a different type used for row badges in the Build, Rooms, Staff and Regime panels. Not this.)

So the architecture already anticipated that a prison might have something neutral to say, reserved a severity for it, and no producer was ever written.

## What that explains

Every player-visibility gap found by playing tonight is the same gap:

| Measured | Where |
|---|---|
| The state grant erodes 300 → 260 → 220 → 180 over four days with nothing saying why | #503 |
| A prisoner's sentence ends and they vanish with no notice; no release string exists in the catalogue at all | #503 |
| Five prisoners discharge and the Regime panel then says *"Nobody has been admitted yet"* | #506 |
| An assault, a riot and an escape attempt are indistinguishable | #506 |
| Which participant was sanctioned to solitary, and why | ADR 0067, "What the player must be told" |

None of these is a refusal and none is a fault. They are **events**, and there is structurally nowhere to put an event. Each has been recorded separately, as its own deferred wording decision, in its own ADR.

## Update — two of the five are now closed, and the strongest evidence yet arrived

Since this was filed:

- **The Regime falsehood is fixed** (PR #508) — and notably **without new copy**, by suppressing the note rather than replacing it. That is worth knowing here because it shows some of these are reachable as *state* fixes and do not need the event channel at all.
- **The incident kind is now named** (PR #509) — using the `IncidentType` labels the content catalogue already shipped with zero call sites. Reporting a computed truth through an already-authored label turned out not to need the owner at all.

So three remain, and all three are genuinely event-shaped.

**And a playtest has now produced the sharpest instance of the problem.** An agent built a prison *specifically* to expose ADR 0067's solitary sanction — two cells, a solitary cell, a canteen, no shower, no yard, zero guards, matching the exact unguarded row of the flashpoint ladder that the ADR says fires. **It fired**: two incidents opened and closed within about a day of admission.

It still could not observe whether a sanction happened. Not whether an incident was a terminal adjudicated assault rather than a riot; not whether `solitarySanctionEndTick` was ever written; not whether anyone was relocated into the solitary cell built for exactly that purpose.

The care in that report is worth repeating, because it is what makes it evidence rather than an impression: `funds` never moved, and that was reported as **inconclusive rather than as a null result** — the neglected setup already left `hygiene` and `recreation` permanently unmet, and those are the *same two needs* `HIGH_RISK_REGIME` additionally restricts (ADR 0067 decision 2), so even a real sanction would have had zero marginal income effect in that configuration.

*"I built a prison specifically to expose this mechanic and still could not observe it happening"* is a stronger statement of this issue than the general case, and it is now on the record.

## Why this is worth deciding as one thing

It reframes what looked like five copy decisions into one architectural question with a wording tail:

> **Should the prison narrate what happens to it, and if so, through the alerts list?**

If the answer is yes, the plumbing is smaller than it looks — the view model, the severity, the rendering, the folding section, the empty-state row and the insertion logic all exist and are used. What is missing is a producer, and a decision about which simulation events are worth a row.

If the answer is no, then `'info'` should be removed from `HudSeverity` and the reason recorded, because a member no producer can reach is a standing invitation to assume the feature exists.

**Either answer is better than the current state**, which is that several documents each defer the same question in their own words.

## What is not proposed here

**No wording**, and no decision. Both the channel's existence (architecture — this would want an ADR) and the sentences themselves (`AGENTS.md`'s fourth exclusion) are the owner's. This issue exists to put the deferrals in one place and show that they are one question, so it can be answered once.

One caution worth stating: `src/ui/simulation-alerts.ts`'s own header comment explains at length why a refusal is *not* a label, and why refusal keys are authored under `hud.alert.refusal.*` rather than derived through `src/content/simulation-message-keys.ts` — *"short, neutral, HUD-appropriate: these are dense panel labels, not prose"*. An event notice is a third kind of thing again, and whichever way this goes, that distinction should survive rather than being collapsed.

PR #508's author independently reached the same boundary from the other side, and their reasoning is worth carrying into the decision: building a discharge *notice* through the alerts channel is event-shaped rather than state-shaped, and would need **both** a new alert-union member and new wording — a second instance of the same owner's-call boundary, on a larger architectural surface.

Related: #503, #506, ADR 0057 open question 1, ADR 0061, ADR 0064, ADR 0067.
