items.title: [Construction] No surface can issue a `PurchaseMaterials` command, so a build order still cannot complete
items.body:
> **Correction — 2026-08-24.** Re-verified line by line against `main` at `9b6965a` (v0.0.16). **The symptom still reproduces; the stated cause no longer holds, and three supporting claims are refuted.** #249 and #250 closed the *last* link of the supply chain — a purchase now deposits into the very `Container` that `ConstructionSystem` draws from — so the chain breaks one link earlier, at the player's end. The title and the "Why" section are rewritten to the link that is actually missing; the three refuted claims are deleted rather than left to mislead, each named below with what is true in its place. Everything else is as filed.
>
> Deleted, with the correction:
> - *"`BUILDABLE_REGISTRY` requires item ids `brick` / `wood-plank`; `src/content/item-catalog.ts` declares `item.brick` / `item.wood-plank`. Two vocabularies that have never met…"* — **fixed in #97.** `src/simulation/construction/definition.ts:24` reads `materialsRequired: [{ itemId: 'item.brick', quantity: 2 }]`, and `:45-46` records the old split in the past tense.
> - *"`ConstructionSystem.cancelOrder` carries a `// TODO: release materials`."* — **implemented.** `src/simulation/construction/system.ts:246` is `this.materialsProvider.release(order.materialsAllocated);`. The only surviving occurrence of that TODO string is inside a comment at `src/simulation/construction/materials-provider.ts:17` describing the former state.
> - *"There is no money in this repository and none should be introduced here."* — **refuted by #249.** `src/simulation/economy/` ships `treasury.ts` and `procurement.ts`, and #250 put the treasury balance on the HUD status strip.
>
> **State note, for the owner rather than acted on here:** this issue is currently *closed* (by PR #262, the documentation sweep), while on that same commit `tests/foundation/unconsumed-command-contract.test.ts:90-91` still records `PurchaseMaterials` as *"#89, unchanged in symptom and changed in cause"*.

## What happens

Place a build order in a real session — through the HUD build panel, `WorkerStateMachine`'s `simulation/initialize` `{kind: 'new'}` path, or `InProcessSessionHost.startNew` — and it reaches `materials-pending` and stays there forever. No wall is ever built, no geometry is ever written, no room is ever enclosed. The core loop cannot complete.

## Why — the link that is actually missing

**Nothing in `src/` can construct a `PurchaseMaterials` command.**

```
$ grep -rn "type: 'PurchaseMaterials'" src/ tests/
tests/integration/economy-build-loop.test.ts:94
tests/unit/protocol-commands-purchase.test.ts:44
```

Two hits, both tests. `HudIntent` (`src/ui/hud/hud.ts:128`) has five members — `select-tab`, `set-clock`, `toggle-panel`, `place-build-order`, `arm-build-tool` — and none of them is a purchase. The command is declared, schema-bounded and handled; it is reachable only from the suite.

Compounding it: #250 put the treasury balance on the status strip, so a player now *sees* money they cannot spend.

## Why the original cause no longer applies

The original diagnosis was that nothing ever deposits into the construction-materials container and *"there is no route by which materials enter a prison"*. There is one now, and it is wired by default:

- `src/simulation/runtime/new-session.ts:193-195` registers the `Container` under `CONSTRUCTION_MATERIALS_CONTAINER_ID` and wires a `ContainerMaterialsProvider` over it into `ConstructionSystem`.
- `:208` constructs `new ProcurementSystem(treasury, constructionMaterials)` — passing **that same container object** as the delivery destination.
- `src/simulation/economy/procurement.ts:167` is `this.destination.deposit(delivery.itemId, delivery.quantity);`.

So a purchase spends now and delivers later into exactly the store construction draws from, and object identity survives a snapshot restore. What is missing is the player's ability to make the purchase at all.

`ConstructionSystem.update` still calls `materialsProvider.tryAllocate(def.materialsRequired)` on every scheduled tick while an order is `materials-pending`, and against a container nothing can fill, that returns `false` forever — the same observable end state, one link further up.

## The decided fix

**A quantity stepper on the Build panel.** Recorded by the owner in ADR 0017 (`docs/adr/0017-money-primary-resource-model.md:161`: *"The owner has decided the surface: a quantity stepper on the Build panel."*). The remaining open half is whether a refused purchase is reported to the player.

⚠️ **Warning for whoever implements it.** `tests/foundation/unconsumed-command-contract.test.ts` holds a `PurchaseMaterials` entry in `AWAITING_PRODUCER` (`:90-91`). That gate fails as **stale** the moment the command gains a producer — `:179-180`, *"these commands now have a producer in `src/`: delete their `AWAITING_PRODUCER` entries in the same change"*. **The entry must be deleted in the same change that adds the stepper**, not in a follow-up.

## Not in scope

Deliveries, shipments and any renewable supply need something able to refuse them, which is #29's economy — the slice of it that exists is `src/simulation/economy/`, and the ledger, grants and recurring costs remain #29's.

items.title: [Hygiene] Repository sweep findings: docs, ADRs, CI gates, duplicated logic, dead code, archive candidates
items.body:
Recorded before the session's container is reclaimed. Four agents swept the repository; the agent that was going to file these as individual issues was stopped by a usage limit mid-run, so this is the raw harvest rather than the tidy split.

**Read this as a work list to be split, not as one work item.** Each numbered block below is roughly one issue's worth. Every claim was cited at `path:line` by the sweeping agent against commit `99f3151`; **`main` has moved since (now `06e187c`), so re-confirm each line number before acting.** Anything you cannot confirm should be dropped, not fixed with a hedge.

## 1. Duplicate ADR number 0004 — highest priority in this list

**Two Accepted ADRs both numbered 0004:** `docs/adr/0004-chunk-size-selection.md` and `docs/adr/0004-deterministic-kernel.md`. The chunk-size ADR was authored first (`cfa2b44`, 2026-08-22 21:00); the deterministic-kernel ADR took the same number 23 minutes later (`aae2fbc`, 21:23).

In a repository whose contract says *"do not invent replacement architecture when an ADR already exists"*, an ambiguous citation namespace is a real hazard, not a cosmetic one — "see ADR 0004" no longer identifies a document. Grep `"ADR 0004"`, `"adr/0004"`, `"0004-"` across the repo to find which citations are now ambiguous.

Related: **no ADR 0017 exists anywhere** — not on `main`, not on any branch, and the string `0017` appears in no file. PR #91 nevertheless claims 0018, skipping it. And ADR 0019 was claimed by the #93 branch. The next free number needs to be unambiguous before anyone writes one.

## 2. ADR statuses that contradict the code

The highest-value check in this area: an ADR marked **Proposed whose decision the code already implements** means the code decided without approval; **Accepted whose decision the code does not implement** is the reverse.

- **ADR 0016** (migration delivery) is the sharpest case: it exists to *seek approval* for a mechanism that is **already switched on and has already fired**. Its decision §1 describes the Supabase GitHub integration as a proposal, while `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` documents it as live since 2026-08-23 with observed evidence.
- **ADR 0006** `:14` — claims the `'ready'` state is entered. `'ready'` is declared in the `WorkerState` union (`src/simulation/worker/state-machine.ts:22`) and **never entered**: every `transition()` call targets something else (`'faulted'` at :90, `'paused'` at :196, `'paused'`/`'running'` at :217, `'shutting-down'` at :315).
- **ADR 0012** `:27` — both the "Minted by" and "Snapshotted?" cells are now wrong, and the ADR's own escape clause has already triggered: `carryItemJobSchema` carries `pathRequestId` (`src/persistence/save-schema.ts:350`, again at `:399`). See #112, which asks for this ADR to be Accepted with the reset-per-recompute decision.
- **ADR 0015** `:167` — every item on its to-do list is done on `main` (the stream is registered at `new-session.ts:159`, the registry constructed at `:169`, passed through at `:171`). Also `:36` claims five subsystems are "not persisted at all"; issue #70's V3 payload carries them via `simulation: sessionSystemsV3Schema.optional()` (`save-schema.ts:710`).
- **ADR 0011** is Accepted and its runtime shipped (`src/services/localization/` has catalog, default-catalog, format, locale, localizer, pseudo), but `src/simulation/rooms/definition.ts:51` still describes it as pending.

**Also produce, as part of this work, the plain list of every currently-Proposed ADR.** The owner needs to know which architectural decisions are queued for them; that list is directly actionable and does not exist anywhere today.

## 3. `README.md:75` claims all ADRs are accepted — five are not

`0012` ("Proposed. Extended by ADR 0015"), `0013` ("**Proposed — pending human approval.** Not accepted."), `0014` ("Status: Proposed"), `0015` ("Proposed. Extends ADR 0012") and `0016`. Small, exact, and it is the repository's front door.

## 4. Docs that are false or stale against the code

- **`docs/WORLD.md:50` — the most consequential.** It states *"returns true if the tile falls within **any** owned parcel or directly owned chunk"*. That is the **renderer's** rule, not the simulation's: `SparseWorld.isTileOwned` resolves exactly one parcel (the first in ascending-id order) and consults only that one. So the documentation has silently taken a side in issue #93. Branch `claude/parcel-ownership-rule` is fixing #93 and touches this section — coordinate rather than duplicating.
- **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:114`** — *"nothing in it runs on the tick or frame path; every call is asynchronous, failable and optional"*. False: `ARCHITECTURE.md:109` lists the localization runtime in `src/services/`, and every entry point (`format`, `formatPlural`, `formatNumber`, `formatDate`, `has`) is **synchronous**, called from the HUD repaint path (`src/ui/hud/status-strip.ts:177-178`). `TelemetryRecorder.record` is synchronous too. The real constraint this hides: a synchronous formatter on the repaint path must stay allocation-cheap.
- **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:31-34` and `:83`** — aspirational stated as present tense. Nothing in `src/` compresses anything; `grep -rn 'compress\|gzip\|deflate\|CompressionStream' src/` returns only the comment describing it as a future backend's decision.
- **`docs/NAVIGATION.md:37-40`** — stale since #74 (`290c0fe`). It says `finalizeConstruction` "only bumps the geometry revision"; it now writes `WALL_EDGE_NUMERIC_ID` into the chunk's edge layer. `RENDERING.md` and `WORLD.md` were updated for #74 and this file was not, so three docs now disagree. (The outer claim that *door* placement is still unwired remains true, because `'door-wooden'` is `category: 'object'` so `edgeNumericIdFor` returns 0.)
- **`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:219`/`:213` vs `:142`/`:146`** — internal contradiction: the same document says the staging Worker serves the public apex domain and, seventy lines later, that staging is confined to `workers.dev` and should be locked behind Cloudflare Access. Both cannot be acted on — putting Access in front of `lockstate-staging` would gate the public site.
- **`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:225-231`** — contradicts ADR 0014: it says mutable stable-name files do not go under `/assets/`, while the entire runtime atlas set does, deliberately, which is why `_headers` carries an exclusive `/assets/actors/*` revalidation rule.
- **`docs/CLOUD_SAVE.md:419-420`** — contradicts itself 388 lines earlier about `pnpm verify:stack` and the service-role key.
- **`docs/PERSISTENCE.md:924-929`** — overstates the `pagehide` safety net (this is #92; branch `claude/lifecycle-pagehide-target` touches it).
- **`docs/ISSUE_BACKLOG.md:16-30`** — the "stable index of the intended dependency order" now indexes **only closed work**: every issue it names (#5, #6, #10–#26) is closed. It stops at phase 7 while `ROADMAP.md` defines phases 8–11, and omits every issue actually in flight.
- **`docs/TESTING.md:81`** — a bundle size (1,384.01 kB) presented with no "at the time" qualifier; `PERSISTENCE.md` records the same figure as the *pre*-wiring bundle, since grown ~16%.
- **`docs/ROADMAP.md:6` and `:11`** — list a linter and formatter and a PR template in Phase 0. **None exists**: no eslint/prettier/biome/oxlint/dprint dependency, no lint script, no lint step in any workflow, and no PR template.
- **`docs/research/ARCHITECTURE_PATTERN_AUDIT.md:17`** names `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` as the mechanism for recording adapted third-party code. That file does not exist.

## 5. Duplicated logic that can drift

This is the pattern that produced #93 and the `'brick'`/`'item.brick'` split, so treat it as a class rather than a list of nits.

- **`src/simulation/presentation/view-model.ts:107` vs `src/ui/primitives/segmented-bar.ts:28`** — two implementations of "how many segments of a bounded bar are lit", returning **different answers**. The projection quantises through an integer permille then floors; the primitive divides directly and ceils. They disagree for **every small-but-nonzero value**, which is precisely the case that matters visually.
- **`src/simulation/rooms/system.ts:44-46` vs `src/simulation/presentation/room-projection.ts:170-181`** — two evaluators of "does this room satisfy its catalog requirements", answering differently. `RoomSystem.validateRoom` unconditionally reports every object requirement as missing and treats `minimum-size` as always satisfied; `requirementStatus` performs a real capability check.
- **`src/simulation/world/sparse-world.ts:127-144` vs `src/simulation/entity/entity-codec.ts:69-80`** — one RLE *shape* in the save, two RLE *implementations*, validating differently. `decodeTerrainRle` rejects out-of-range values and non-positive counts with typed errors; the other does not. (See #102, where exactly this class of missing bound is the defect.)
- **The clock speed ladder is spelled independently in at least five places across four layers** — `src/ui/hud/view-model.ts:25`, `src/simulation/clock/fixed-step-clock.ts:1`, `src/simulation/protocol/types.ts:139`, `src/main.ts:277`, `src/ui/simulation-commands.ts:70,159,222` — three of them as inline `1 | 2 | 4` type literals rather than references. Adding a ×8 speed means finding all five. The comparable case next door was handled properly (`HUD_BUILD_EDGES`), so the right shape already exists in the codebase.
- **`src/simulation/rooms/definition.ts:60`** — `roomDefinitionFromCatalog` resolves localization keys into **English display strings** and stores them on `RoomDefinition.name`, inside the simulation layer. `src/main.ts` states the opposite rule as its reason for maintaining `BUILDABLE_LABEL_KEY`, and ADR 0011's whole point is that translated text is the HUD's business.
- **The Node version is pinned literally in three files** — `.node-version` (the real source of truth, read by CI at three points), `tests/foundation/repository-contract.test.ts:43` (intentional, so a bump fails the suite), and `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh:28` (not intentional).

## 6. Tests that cannot fail, or test something other than their title

- **`tests/contract/art-pipeline-contract.test.ts:67-79`** — the title claims content hashing; the body proves only that the sha256 field is 64 hex characters and that a file exists at the declared path. **It never reads the image bytes and never recomputes the digest**, so `source-art.v1.json` could declare any well-formed hash for any image and the test would pass.
- **`tests/unit/prisoners-regime.test.ts:12-18`** — samples 18 of 2,400 ticks (stride 137) and asserts only that no throw occurs. Never asserts full coverage, never asserts "exactly once", never inspects the returned block. Also redundant: the real gate is the module-load validator.
- **`tests/unit/ui-async-action-gate.test.ts:23-25`** — points at `tests/browser/save-panel-concurrency.spec.ts`, which **does not exist**. The coverage does exist (in `ui-shell.spec.ts:33-34`), so this is a stale filename, not missing coverage — but it is the only thing telling a reader where to look.
- **`src/content/room-catalog.ts:22-28`** names `room-catalog-adapter.ts`, which **has never existed**. The conversion is done by `roomDefinitionFromCatalog`.
- **The flaky determinism test.** `tests/unit/prisoners-operations-scenario.test.ts` → "an identical seed and scenario produce an identical fingerprint" needs ~6 s under CPU load against `vitest.config.ts:14`'s `testTimeout: 5_000`. It passes in isolation (7/7 in ~8–13 s total) and **fails on `main` too**, so it is not caused by any current branch. **It matters because of *how* it fails:** a timeout inside a determinism test is reported as a *determinism failure*, which in this repository is the most alarming possible false positive. Either raise the timeout for that test, split it, or make it cheaper — but do not leave it looking like non-determinism.

## 7. CI gates weaker than they look

- **The fork guard makes required checks satisfiable by skipping.** All three jobs carry the identical guard (`ci.yml:22`, `:90`, `:217`) and chain by `needs` (`assets` needs `verify`, `browser` needs `assets`). A PR from a fork therefore produces three **skipped** jobs — and GitHub counts a skipped required check as satisfied. Harmless today (solo repo, no forks); **a hole from day one the moment branch protection is enabled.** Test with one real fork PR before trusting the gate.
- **`pnpm verify:stack` is in no gate at all.** `grep -rn 'verify:stack|verify-supabase-stack' .github/` returns nothing. It is the repository's strongest Supabase check and, per #105, the **only** thing that verifies the identity step every RLS policy depends on — that PostgREST maps a token to `authenticated` with the right `sub`, and that anonymous sign-in yields a usable identity. It needs Docker, which is why it is ungated; but that means the foundation of the whole schema is verified only when a human remembers.
- **Three of four security headers are asserted by nothing.** `public/_headers:2-5` sets four; only `nosniff` is verified end-to-end (`scripts/verify-deployment-preview.mjs:208-210`). Deleting `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy` and `Permissions-Policy` leaves `pnpm verify`, `pnpm verify:deployment` and all three CI jobs green. (#105 adds that there is no CSP at all, which matters because Phaser is 1.6 MB of unaudited bundled code.)
- **`.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` provisions two of the four CI gates.** It never calls `scripts/provision-git-lfs.sh`, never runs `git lfs pull`, and never calls `scripts/provision-playwright-browsers.sh` — both scripts exist and CI invokes them. So an agent in a web session **cannot run `pnpm verify:assets` at all** and cannot run the browser suite without provisioning it by hand. This is why every session rediscovers the LFS-pointer failure.
- **`.gitattributes:32-33`** pins LF by extension, but the stated rationale is about executable scripts with shebangs. `scripts/verify-supabase-sql.mjs` is mode 755 and starts `#!/usr/bin/env node`, and is covered by **neither** pattern — checked out on Windows with `core.autocrlf=true` it would fail with a bad-interpreter error, exactly the failure the comment describes preventing.
- **`supabase/config.toml:40-42` vs `scripts/provision-postgres.sh:22-27`** — three PostgreSQL majors in play and none reconciled: config pins 17, the provision script is version-agnostic and gave 16.13 here, and the hosted staging project's major is recorded nowhere in the repository.
- **`supabase/config.toml:159`, `:163`, `:66-71`** — untouched `supabase init` defaults describing a project this is not: an auth redirect allow-list pointing at port 3000 (nothing serves it) and seeding enabled against a file that does not exist.

## 8. AGENTS.md violations

**Four bare `any` casts at the main-thread/worker protocol boundary** — `src/simulation/worker/state-machine.ts:29`, `:37`, `:96`, `:308` — precisely the surface `CLAUDE.md` names as needing architectural care. The load-bearing one is **`:96`**: `fault()` accepts `code: string` and casts it into a closed 12-member enum, so **a typo compiles, ships, and only fails at runtime**. AGENTS.md forbids disabling type strictness. (Directly relevant to #103, which proposes changing `fault()`.)

Also **`src/services/entitlements/products.ts:60-61`** — both product `nameKey`s point at keys absent from the only locale catalog. `resolveLocalizationKey` falls back to the key itself, so a storefront built on this would display the literal string `product.save-slots.plus-5.name` **to a paying customer**.

## 9. Dead code and unused content — the majority case, not the exception

- **`src/simulation/presentation/`** — 10 files, 2,349 lines, structurally unreachable. Already filed as **#104**; do not re-file, but note it is the largest item here.
- **The trusted-services and cloud-save layer, ~2,522 lines, imported only by its own tests:** `src/services/telemetry/` (763), `src/services/entitlements/` (883), `src/services/challenges/` (552), `src/persistence/cloud/` (324). `src/main.ts` touches `src/services/` exactly twice, both from `services/localization/`.
- **Catalog entries with no consumer are the majority:** **11 of 18** room ids, **18 of 20** object ids, **5 of 8** staff-role ids are referenced by no code anywhere, production or test. ⚠️ **`room.delivery-bay`, `object.loading-dock-door` and `room.storage-room` are in this set and must NOT be removed** — issues #96 and #99 make them the intended consumers.
- **164 of 166 derived simulation-enum locale keys are never looked up.** The assembled `en` catalog holds ~259 keys; production looks up 54 (the 52 in `HUD_MESSAGE_KEY` plus two build-edge keys derived at `src/ui/hud/build-panel.ts:103`).
- **Eight barrel files with no importer:** `src/persistence/local/index.ts`, `src/persistence/cloud/index.ts`, `src/persistence/session/index.ts`, `src/rendering/build/index.ts`, `src/simulation/worker/index.ts`, `src/ui/primitives/index.ts`, plus `src/persistence/index.ts` and `src/services/index.ts` which are referenced only from prose. Note `src/persistence/cloud/index.ts` is the *only* path by which `supabase-client.ts` is reachable, so removing it orphans that file.
- **`src/input/pointer.ts`, `src/input/accessibility.ts`, and the settings-persistence API** in `src/input/storage.ts` / `settings.ts` — the barrel makes the tree look reachable; production consumes three symbols. `PointerInputAdapter` is never constructed outside tests, and the entire accessibility module is unused.
- **`tsconfig.json:20`** includes `worker-configuration.d.ts`, which **does not exist**, nothing generates, and is not gitignored. It is what `wrangler types` emits for a Worker's `Env` bindings — but `wrangler.jsonc` declares no `main`, so this assets-only Worker has no bindings to type. TypeScript silently ignores an absent listed file, so `tsc -b` stays clean and the entry is invisible.

## 10. Archive candidates

Confidence ratings from the sweeping agent. **Err toward "needs owner judgement"** — recommending deletion of something load-bearing is far worse than leaving something inert.

| path | why | confidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `package.json:26` `smoke:deployment` | strict subset of `verify:deployment`, which is the CI gate; two names invite running the weaker one and believing the gate ran | certain |
| `package.json:14` `build:production` | pure alias of `build`, which already builds production; nothing references it | certain |
| `tsconfig.json:20` entry | see item 9 | certain |
| `test-results/…/error-context.md` | leftover Playwright output from the known LFS failure; correctly gitignored and untracked | certain |
| `src/persistence/local/index.ts`, `session/index.ts`, `rendering/build/index.ts`, `simulation/worker/index.ts`, `ui/primitives/index.ts` | barrels with no importer; every consumer imports the concrete module | likely |
| `public/game-content/source-art/` (23 PNGs) + `source-art.v1.json` | **24 files published to the deployed site and loaded by nothing.** No module in `src/` fetches the catalog or any image under it; the renderer's only asset path is `AtlasLibrary.load()` → `/assets/actors/asset-registry.json`. Duplicates bytes already in `assets/source/` | needs owner judgement |
| `tooling/build-source-art-catalog.mjs` | generates the above; invoked by **nothing** — not `package.json`, not a workflow, not another script. Its only mention is prose in `docs/ART_PIPELINE.md`. So editing an input silently does not regenerate the committed output | needs owner judgement |
| `tooling/blender/create-environment-catalog.py` + `assets/source/blender/environment.mvp.catalog.blend` + `.manifest.json` | a closed loop with no exit: invoked by nothing, documented nowhere. `ART_PIPELINE.md` documents five sibling scripts and never mentions this one | needs owner judgement |
| `docs/research/ARCHITECTURE_PATTERN_AUDIT.md` | a 2026-08-22 audit whose architectural questions have since been settled by accepted ADRs | needs owner judgement |
| `src/persistence/index.ts`, `src/services/index.ts` | barrels referenced only from prose/docstrings | needs owner judgement |

Also check `.gitignore` actually covers generated output (`test-results/`, `benchmark-results/`, build output) — a tracked generated directory is itself a finding.

## What the sweep verified as CORRECT — worth recording

The agent ran these rather than reading them: `pnpm verify:sql` applies all nine migrations in order and passes **89 pgTAP assertions**; `tooling/validate-runtime-atlas.mjs` correctly exits 1 on LFS pointers rather than validating text stubs; `benchmark:smoke` + `verify-benchmark-result.mjs` re-verify 8 deterministic scenarios; the `browser` CI job really does call `scripts/provision-playwright-browsers.sh` (it exists) and really ran the 38-test Playwright suite in run `32661466069`. Every `package.json` script points at a file that exists; `engines`/`packageManager`/`.node-version` agree with what is installed; `wrangler deploy --strict` is a real flag; vitest's include matches all 121 test files with no orphans; `.gitattributes` covers all 56 `.png` and all 6 `.blend` files with no stale LFS pattern; and `.agents/rules/lockstate.md` defers to `AGENTS.md` without diverging.

items.title: [ADR] Audit of the whole ADR corpus (0001–0021 + README): status truth, claim truth, cross-ADR contradictions, number hygiene, dangling references and the owner's open-decision queue
items.body:
Read-only audit of the **entire ADR corpus** — `docs/adr/0001-*.md` … `docs/adr/0021-*.md` plus `docs/adr/README.md` — for drift between what each ADR says and what `main` actually is. No file in `src/`, `tests/` or `docs/` was touched; the deliverable is this issue.

Continuation of **#116**. Overlaps and corrects **#118** (see **C1–C4** and, in particular, **A2**, which falsifies #118's own mitigating sentence).

**Audited at `main` @ `7a15b17` (v0.0.19); every finding re-verified at `main` @ `3f1a144` (v0.0.22)** after #267, #268 and #269 landed mid-audit. **No ADR file changed between the two** and no finding changed. The line numbers below are the ones at `3f1a144`; the ones that moved — all in `src/simulation/runtime/new-session.ts` and `src/simulation/runtime/session-commands.ts` — were re-read from disk rather than adjusted by arithmetic. Every claim below was established from `git log`, `git grep` and the implementation. No sentence from another document, from an issue body, or from a code comment was accepted as evidence — those are the things being audited. Where a claim could only be established from outside the repository it is marked **INFERRED** and says so.

**Verdict vocabulary:** VERIFIED / FALSE for each checkable claim; LIVE / LATENT for each defect; `path:line` plus the quoted text throughout.

---

# 0. Summary

| | count |
| --- | --- |
| ADR files on disk | 20 (`0001`–`0017`, `0019`–`0021`) |
| README rows naming a file | 20, all statuses agreeing with the documents (**mechanically re-run, 7/7 green**) |
| Number-hygiene defects found | **0** |
| Dangling file references found | **0** |
| Fabricated quotations found | **1** (**A4**) |
| Claims examined and ruled on | **A1–A20** — **15 FALSE**, 3 stale-or-imprecise (A11, A16, A17), 2 VERIFIED clean (A18, A20) |
| Of those, **LIVE** | **3** — **A2**, **A6**, **A9** |
| #118 defects re-verified as still live | **4** (C1–C4) |
| #118 claims found FALSE | **1** (**A2** — its stated mitigation does not exist) |
| Absolute "nothing does X" claims checked exhaustively | **18** — 16 VERIFIED, 2 FALSE (A1, A15), plus one implied absolute FALSE (A2) |
| Code changes recommended | **2** — A2 (a decision first) and A17 (two lines) |

The one-directional pattern #118 named still holds and has grown a second head. #118 said *Proposed decisions are already shipped*. The corpus now also shows the mirror: **Accepted ADRs describing mechanisms that no production code path exercises** — the handshake (**A2**), the telemetry sink (**A14**), the challenge layer (**A18**) — and **Accepted ADRs whose guarantee the code has since retracted in a comment while the ADR kept asserting it** (**A3**).

---

# 1. Status truth

`docs/adr/README.md`'s own rule is *"The `Status` column reproduces what each ADR's own document says, not a normalised judgement"*, and `tests/foundation/adr-numbering-contract.test.ts:221` enforces document↔index agreement. **Both hold.** Executed:

```
$ npx vitest run tests/foundation/adr-numbering-contract.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

So no ADR's status disagrees with its own index row. What follows is the other question — whether the status agrees with **`main`**.

| ADR | Status | Settled by | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0001 Core platform | Accepted | `package.json:39` `"phaser": "4.2.1"`, `:48` `"vite": "8.2.2"`, `:6` `"packageManager": "pnpm@11.22.0"`, `tsconfig.json:7` `"strict": true`, `wrangler.jsonc`, `src/persistence/local/indexeddb-store.ts`, `src/main.ts:13` `import SimulationWorker from './simulation/worker/worker.ts?worker'` | **Consistent** |
| 0002 Cloudflare Static Assets | Accepted | `wrangler.jsonc:19-32`, `vite.config.ts:6`, `public/_headers`, `scripts/verify-cloudflare-deployment.mjs:35-37` | **Consistent in configuration; contradicted in operation — see A9** |
| 0003 Worker protocol | Accepted | `src/simulation/protocol/types.ts` in full | **Consistent, except decision 4 — see A2** |
| 0004 Chunk size | Accepted | `src/simulation/runtime/new-session.ts:174` `world = new SparseWorld(32);` | **Consistent — see A17 for a shape complaint** |
| 0005 Entity storage | Accepted | `src/simulation/entity/entity-store.ts:13-15`, `:149` | **Consistent, except the determinism guarantee — see A3** |
| 0006 Worker adapter | Accepted | `src/simulation/worker/state-machine.ts:26-31`, `:190`, `:205` | **Inconsistent — C1, and A2** |
| 0007 Navigation budgets | Accepted | `src/simulation/navigation/navigation-system.ts:35-38`, `new-session.ts:351` | **Consistent — see A4, A5 for prose** |
| 0008 Trusted boundary | Accepted | `tests/unit/services-layer-boundaries.test.ts:147,155,161,171,183`; `20260824090100_revoke_client_truncate.sql`, `20260824150000_revoke_trusted_truncate.sql` | **Consistent** |
| 0009 Challenge verification | Accepted — implementation gated | `src/services/challenges/verification.ts:160`, `:300` | **Consistent, and all four gates are unmet — see A18** |
| 0010 Telemetry privacy | Accepted | `src/services/telemetry/consent.ts:12,33`, `events.ts:80`, `redaction.ts:63` | **Modules consistent; the layer is dead — see A14** |
| 0011 Localization | Accepted | `src/services/localization/`, `tests/unit/services-layer-boundaries.test.ts:161` | **Consistent — see A20** |
| 0012 Derived identifiers | Proposed | `src/simulation/rooms/topology.ts:16,189` | **Taxonomy in use, table wrong — C2** |
| 0013 Free-tier capacity | Proposed — pending human approval | `supabase/migrations/20260823100000_bound_free_tier_capacity.sql` | **§§1-4 implemented ahead of approval; §§5-6 absent — and A6, A7, A8** |
| 0014 Art storage | Proposed | `.gitattributes:1-4`, `public/_headers:61-76`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:155-262` | **Fully implemented ahead of approval — see A15** |
| 0015 Actor identity | Proposed | `new-session.ts:187,198,248`; `save-schema.ts:816` | **Shipped end to end, incl. save format — C3** |
| 0016 Migration delivery | Proposed — pending human approval | `.github/workflows/migrate-database.yml:33,47,64`; `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:139-163` | **Mechanism live and unapproved — C4, and A10, A11** |
| 0017 Money primary | Accepted | `src/simulation/economy/treasury.ts:51`, `procurement.ts:126`, `src/content/procurement-catalog.ts:71-72` | **Consistent** |
| 0019 Tile ownership | Accepted | `src/simulation/world/tile-ownership.ts:61`, `sparse-world.ts:560`, `world-view.ts:232` | **Consistent** |
| 0020 Deterministic kernel | Accepted | `src/simulation/kernel/kernel.ts:113-114`, `:119-137`, `src/simulation/rng/xoshiro128starstar.ts:2-3` | **Consistent** |
| 0021 Security headers | Proposed — pending human approval | `public/_headers:6-10` | **Fully implemented ahead of approval — see A12** |

**The pattern, stated numerically.** Of the six `Proposed` ADRs, **five** (0013 in part, 0014, 0015, 0016, 0021) are implemented on `main`. Of the fourteen `Accepted` ones, **three** describe a mechanism no production path exercises (0003 decision 4, 0009's gated half, 0010's sink) and **two** contain a claim the code has since contradicted (0005, 0006).

---

# 2. Claim truth

Twenty findings, **A1–A20**. The index below is the whole result; **the full evidence for each — the quoted sentence, the `path:line`, the `git` command that settles it, the LIVE/LATENT reasoning and the exact replacement text — is in the first comment on this issue**, which is part of this record and not a supplement to it. It was split out only because the two together exceed GitHub's body limit.

| # | ADR | Verdict | Live? | Claim | Smallest correct fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A1** | ADR 0003 | FALSE | LATENT | `simulation/delta` "was declared in the kind union with **no schema** and no sender" — it has had a full Zod schema since 26 h *before* the amendment was written. | Correct the premise; the conclusion survives. |
| **A2** | ADR 0003 / 0006 | FALSE | **LIVE** | **Nothing in `src/` has ever sent a `protocol/handshake`.** Decision 4's version/capability negotiation happens for nobody, and #118's stated mitigation ("the only client does handshake first") is itself false. | Send the handshake and make `'ready'` a real state — or delete both and amend two ADRs. |
| **A3** | ADR 0005 | FALSE | LATENT | *"Naturally guarantees strictly ascending ID order"* — `query.ts:20-29` says that phrasing "over-claimed" and narrows it to **index** order. | Rewrite the bullet to the guarantee the code gives. |
| **A4** | ADR 0007 | FALSE | LATENT | Quotes *"`SparseWorld` exposes no such enumeration"* from `docs/NAVIGATION.md`. **That string has never been in that file, on any branch.** | Quote the real phrase, or drop the quotation marks. |

- **The escape clause has fired.** ADR 0012 `:313-315` says *"If routing state ever enters a save, they become category 1."* It has. The restore side already compensates by hand: `src/simulation/operations/job.ts:110` `restored.pathRequestId = undefined;` (and `src/simulation/security/guard-roster.ts:198` does the same).

**C3 — ADR 0015's to-do list (still live, every item done).** `docs/adr/0015-…:168-171` still reads *"must register … Until it does, identity is inert"*. On `main`: `new-session.ts:187` registers `ACTOR_IDENTITY_RNG_STREAM`, `:198` passes the registry into `PrisonerOperationsRuntime`, `:248` gives `GuardRoster` the minter. `:102` (*"the envelope field is #70's to add"*) and `:167` (*"This ADR deliberately does not create the V3 bump"*) are both overtaken by `save-schema.ts:678` and `:816`. And `:40` — *"prisoners, staff, security, contraband and incidents are not persisted at all"* — is contradicted by `sessionSystemsV3Schema` (`save-schema.ts:769-775`), which persists `prisoners, operations, navigation, security, contraband, incidents`, plus `economy` at `:775`.

**C4 — ADR 0016's status (still live).** Covered as **Q1**.

---

# 8. Recommended order of work

1. **A9 / Q9** — the ADR 0002 warning note. Five lines of prose; removes a trap that silently moves a live domain.
2. **A2 / Q4** — decide the handshake, then implement. It is the only finding whose fix makes two Accepted ADRs true at once, and it comes with a missing test that would also close A1.
3. **A6 / Q2 and A7 / Q3** — correct ADR 0013's two false derivations *before* the owner is asked to sign the three numbers. Asking for approval on arithmetic that is wrong by 144× is worse than not asking.
4. **A3** — ADR 0005's determinism sentence. One sentence; it stops the corpus contradicting `src/simulation/entity/query.ts`, and it is on the direct path to #31.
5. **C1–C4** — #118's four, unchanged, now with A2 folded into C1.
6. **A1, A4, A5, A8, A10–A16, A19, plus X4's one clause** — the prose sweep. Every one has its exact replacement text in the comment below; they are one commit.
7. **A17** — the only code-shape fix: `DEFAULT_TILE_CHUNK_SIZE = 32` beside `WORLD_CHUNK_SIZE_LIMIT`.
8. **The missing contract test.** `tests/foundation/unconsumed-message-kind-contract.test.ts`, in the shape of `unconsumed-command-contract.test.ts` and `fault-code-reachability-contract.test.ts`, asserting that every member of `MAIN_TO_WORKER_MESSAGE_KINDS` and `WORKER_TO_MAIN_MESSAGE_KINDS` has a producer in `src/` or an allow-list entry with a stated reason. It catches **A1** and **A2** together and is the one structural gap this audit found.

**Surviving mutations, named so they can be run.** Delete `'ready'` from `WorkerState` → the whole suite stays green. Delete `handleHandshake` entirely → green. Delete the `deltaMessageSchema` member from `workerToMainMessageSchema` → green in `src/` (only `tests/contract/` notices). Each is the concrete demonstration that the corresponding ADR sentence is guarded by nothing.

items.title: [Protocol] What the second slice through the projection channel hits: no page-request direction, and two accessors that cannot be published on a timer
items.body:
> **Corrected — 2026-08-24.** Re-verified against `main` at `9b6965a` (v0.0.16). Items 1, 3 and 4 hold exactly as filed. **Two claims were false and are corrected in place:**
>
> - Item 2's first bullet said *"Publishing this needs a non-draining accessor first."* **One already exists and is already the documented contract.** `src/simulation/contraband/confiscation.ts:36-38` is `public all(): readonly ConfiscationEvent[]` under the comment *"Chronological (append) order — read-only, does not consume"*, and `src/simulation/presentation/contraband-projection.ts:42` already types its source as that accessor: *"Read-only; never `drain()`, which would consume the evidence a panel is showing."* The open half is the sentence that followed — **who drains, and when** — and it is more open than this issue implied: `grep -nF "drain(" src/ tests/` returns exactly two lines, the declaration and that comment. **Nothing calls `drain()` at all**, in `src/` or in the suite.
> - Item 5 said `simulation/delta` has *"no schema and no sender."* **The schema exists.** `src/simulation/protocol/types.ts:400-420` defines `deltaMessageSchema` with a `superRefine` enforcing `tick > baseTick`, and it is in the union at `:576`. **No sender remains true**, and so does everything item 5 says about what adopting it would require.

#104's MVP landed in #156: `simulation/status-counts`, worker→main, ten integers, 500 ms ceiling, skipped when unchanged. It needed **no protocol change at all** — which is exactly why it fitted. The next slice does not have that property, and these are the four things it runs into. Filed now, while the reasons are measured rather than remembered.

None of these is a defect in what landed. They are the reasons the MVP was the right first slice.

## 1. The protocol has no direction for "ask for a page"

`docs/HUD_PROJECTIONS.md` contract 5 requires paging: a projection takes `offset`/`limit` rather than returning an unbounded list. But `MAIN_TO_WORKER_MESSAGE_KINDS` (`src/simulation/protocol/types.ts`) has **no kind that requests a projection**, so those two inputs have nowhere to come from. A roster or incident publication today would have to either push the whole list or let the worker choose the window — and a worker-chosen window is not paging, it is truncation the UI cannot scroll.

So the roster slice needs a main→worker request kind before it needs a payload. That is an ADR 0003 shape question (a correlated request/response pair, `optionallyCorrelatedEnvelopeFields`, versus the uncorrelated publication the counts use), not an implementation detail.

The counts needed neither `offset` nor `limit`, because ten integers are not a list. That is the whole reason the MVP fitted inside today's protocol.

## 2. Two projection sources are unsafe to read on a timer

Both are **mutating or unbounded reads**, and a cadence-driven publication would hit them twice a second:

- **`ConfiscationLedger.drain()` empties the ledger.** A publication that called it would blank the contraband panel and *discard the state it was trying to report*. The panel would show one publication's worth of confiscations and then nothing. **The accessor to publish through already exists** — `confiscation.ts:36-38`'s non-consuming `all()`, which `contraband-projection.ts:42` already requires. **What is open is the other half: who drains, and when.** As of `9b6965a` nothing calls `drain()` anywhere, including the tests, so the ledger currently grows for the life of a session and the draining consumer this method was written for has never been named. Publishing the panel does not force that decision, but leaving it undecided means the "unbounded read" problem in the next bullet applies to this ledger too, eventually.
- **`IncidentLog.all()` materialises every incident ever recorded** (`src/simulation/incidents/incident.ts:189`). So a timer-driven incident-history publication is O(all incidents) per send, growing without bound over a session — the firehose #104 names, arriving through the payload size rather than the send rate.

The counts read `.length`-shaped facts and a `Uint8Array` liveness scan, which is why the measured payload is a constant ~229 bytes at 250 and at 5,000 actors.

## 3. `statusCountsEqual` does not generalise

Field-by-field comparison is right for ten integers and measurably cheap. "Publish only what changed" over *rows* is a different problem: a deep compare of a 250-row roster twice a second costs more than the send it avoids. That wants a **revision counter on the source registry** — incremented on mutation, compared as one integer — not a structural diff at the boundary.

Worth deciding before the second consumer copies the first one's pattern.

## 4. No cell-only capacity exists

The status strip renders an occupancy bar with over-capacity tones. `roomCapacity` is the sum over *all* room instances, so it is not the denominator the bar means, and #156 deliberately left `prisonerCapacity` reporting what the projection actually has rather than inventing a number. Until the simulation can answer "how many prisoners can be housed", that bar and its tones stay unreachable regardless of the channel.

## 5. `simulation/delta` has a schema, and still no sender

Corrected: the schema landed. `src/simulation/protocol/types.ts:400-420` is `deltaMessageSchema` — `baseTick`, `tick`, `delta: versionedPayloadSchema`, `.strict()`, with a `superRefine` that rejects `tick <= baseTick` — and it is a member of the decode union at `:576`. So the base-tick *invariant* is already expressed and enforced at the boundary.

What is unchanged, and is the actual remainder: **nothing sends one.** It was deliberately not adopted by #156, because a counts readout is a **level**, not a diff from a base tick. If the roster slice does want diffs, what it still needs is a sender, a base-tick *contract* (which tick a receiver is expected to hold, and how it says so), and an answer for what a receiver does when it missed the base — none of which the counts required, and none of which a schema supplies.

Refs #104, #156, #94. Governed by ADR 0003; `docs/HUD_PROJECTIONS.md` contract 5.

items.title: [Continuation prompt] START HERE — complete brief for the next model taking over Lockstate
items.body:
**This is the entry point.** Hand the next model this issue's URL, or paste the prompt below. Written 2026-08-23 ~23:40 as the previous session's 5-hour usage budget ran out with three workflows stopped mid-flight. Nothing is lost — everything durable is on GitHub, and this issue says exactly where each unfinished thread stops.

---

# The prompt

You are taking over work on **Lockstate**, a browser-based prison management simulation at `https://lockstate.io`. The previous session ran out of usage budget and deliberately stopped its agents at stage boundaries so no work would be wasted. Everything it learned is in GitHub issues. **Do not re-derive it.**

## Read these first, in order, before touching anything

1. **`AGENTS.md`** — the binding agent contract. `CLAUDE.md` points back to it. Not optional.
2. **Issue #107** — the session handover: production state, every open PR with its blocking question, environment facts, and "things that bit and will bite again".
3. **This issue's "Where each thread stops"** section below — the precise resume points.
4. **Issue #95** — the earlier handover. Still authoritative for deployment topology and the secret layout; #107 supersedes the rest.

## The three most urgent things

### 1. #115 — the build cursor does not match where the wall lands

**A live, owner-reported bug that makes the game's core interaction unusable.** The diagnosis is complete and verified in #115: `screenToWorld` (`src/rendering/camera/coordinates.ts:47`) models zoom as scaling about the viewport **top-left**; Phaser scales about the **centre** (`originX`/`originY` both default to `0.5`, `BaseCamera.js:467` and `:484`, and `getWorldPoint` inverts the full camera matrix). They differ by `origin × (1/zoom − 1)` — **exactly zero at zoom 1**, half a screen at zoom 0.5.

That zero is why it shipped: the app starts at zoom 1 because nothing calls `setZoom` at init, so the tool is correct until the player touches the scroll wheel. Anyone who tested without zooming saw it work.

**Branch `claude/fix-cursor-world-offset` exists locally but nothing was pushed** — the agent proving it in a browser was stopped mid-run. Start from #115's analysis, which is complete, and do the work: prove it in a real browser against a real Phaser camera, fix it, and add a test that compares the pure functions against a real camera.

**Note the signature change:** the correct maths needs the viewport size to compute the origin, and `CameraState` does not carry it. Callers to update: `worldPointOf` (`world-scene.ts:290`), the wheel handler (`:141`), the touch pinch (`:187`), `previewHover` (`:368`), plus `zoomAtScreenPoint` and `visibleWorldBounds`. Also decide, with a stated reason, whether to keep the pure functions at all or delegate to `camera.getWorldPoint`.

### 2. #125 — three branches need their review findings applied before any PR

`claude/fix-save-panel-overlap` (#88), `claude/lifecycle-pagehide-target` (#92) and `claude/parcel-ownership-rule` (#93) all carry **complete, green, pushed work** whose adversarial-review findings were **not** applied. #125 has every finding with measurements. The previous session deliberately withheld PRs for these three. One is `blocking`: the #93 branch repeats a **fabricated** player-impact story in five places, and `canBuildAt` has zero callers in `src/`.

`claude/hud-clock-transport` (PR #94) **did** get its fixes applied and pushed (`538bf93`) — it is in good shape and needs nothing from #125.

### 3. #89 / #96 — nothing can be built, and that is now a product consequence

No build order can complete because nothing supplies materials. The owner decided (**#96**) that money is the primary currency and materials are **purchased and delivered**, and deliberately **held #91's starting stock** until the economy exists. So the critical path to a playable session is a minimal slice of **#29**: money, a purchase, a delivery into the bay. Everything after the delivery already exists and is tested.

## Owner decisions — settled, do not relitigate

- **#96** Money is the primary currency. Materials are **bought and delivered**, never gathered or produced. The state pays the operator per head. There is no resource-gathering fantasy in this game.
- **#99** Removing a built object **dismantles** it into salvage that must be **carried to a storeroom** — not destroyed, not instantly refunded.
- **#91's starting stock is held.** That is why #97 exists: it splits out the two correctness fixes that should not wait.

`room.delivery-bay`, `object.loading-dock-door` and `room.storage-room` already exist in the content catalogs and are read by no code. Both decisions are about **connecting declared content**, not inventing subsystems. **Do not delete them** as dead content (see #124).

## Two things you cannot do — they need the owner

Verified with the actual tools, not assumed: there is **no** GitHub MCP tool for branch protection or rulesets, no `gh` CLI in this environment, and repository settings cannot be pushed with git. The permission classifier also blocks `git push --delete` and `gh secret set`.

1. **Branch protection on `main` is OFF** — GitHub's own banner confirms it. Ask the owner to require a PR plus checks `verify`, `assets`, `browser` (exact job names) and "branches up to date before merging". **Warn them about the fork trap** (#124 item 7): all three jobs share a fork guard and chain by `needs`, so a fork PR produces three *skipped* jobs — and GitHub counts a skipped required check as **satisfied**.
2. **The Supabase auto-migration path.** A merge to `main` applies migrations through Supabase's own GitHub integration, configured in their dashboard, invisible from the repo, and triggered by the merge rather than by any migration file changing (`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:136` has the proof). Nothing here can gate it, which is why ADR 0016 §2 is unenforceable from the repository.

Also worth asking them to run, from #105: **`\dp public.*`** on the hosted project (confirms the TRUNCATE finding before acting), **`\dn+ public`** (whether `authenticated` holds CREATE on schema `public`), and whether **`/auth/v1/signup` is rate-limited** — ADR 0013 §7 records that as unimplemented and it is the multiplier on every capacity finding.

## Where each thread stops — resume points

| thread | state | resume at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Camera cursor fix** | diagnosis complete in #115; branch created, **nothing pushed** | #115, then prove-in-browser → fix → test |
| **Review fixes for #88/#92/#93** | findings recorded in **#125**, **not applied**; branches hold original green work | #125, one branch at a time |
| **Review fixes for #94** | ✅ applied and pushed (`538bf93`) | nothing |
| **Audit verification** | ✅ complete — 7 findings filed (#106, #108–#113), 1 refuted (#114) | nothing |
| **Security audit** | ✅ complete and executed — **#105** | act on its findings; the owner checks above |
| **Hygiene sweep** | agent filed #117–#123 before being stopped; the rest is in **#124** | split #124 into work items |
| **Feature research** | ✅ complete; its top recommendation is **#104** | #104 first |
| **PRs #97, #98, #100, #101** | ✅ ready, unmerged | review and merge |

**⚠️ One risk that must not be lost:** after merging **#100**, confirm a `Deploy` run appears *triggered by that CI run* and that lockstate.io reflects the new commit. `workflow_run` triggers are read from the file on the **default branch**, so the change's first real test is its own merge — and if it is wrong, **the site silently stops deploying** and nothing announces it. If no `Deploy` run appears, revert `deploy.yml`.

## Working practices this repository specifically demands

Each of these is here because it already went wrong:

- **Doc-truth regressions are the dominant defect class.** PR #90 removed 18 false claims across 29 locations. **All four** code tracks in the last session re-introduced some, and all four adversarial reviews came back `needs_work` with findings that were almost entirely false or overstated claims in comments, docstrings and ADRs — **not logic bugs**. Before finishing any change, re-read every comment and doc sentence your diff touches and confirm it is still true.
- **The cautionary example:** a branch fixing #93 repeated a fabricated player-impact story in *five places*. `canBuildAt` has zero callers. **Do not invent consequences to justify a fix** — the honest reason is almost always sufficient, and inventing one makes the case weaker, not stronger.
- **A green suite is not a guarded suite.** For every behaviour you add, name a one-line mutation to your own implementation and *run it* to confirm a test fails. #115 exists because `tests/unit/camera-coordinates.test.ts:9` round-trips a function against its own inverse — which passes for *any* invertible transform, including a wrong one. #94's headline behaviour had no headless guard at all: mutating `UNKNOWN_HUD_CLOCK.day` from 0 to 1 left all 1183 unit tests green.
- **Verify, do not assume.** An external audit marked a finding CONFIRMED that does not exist (#114 records the refutation so nobody re-fixes a non-bug). A security agent nearly produced a false clean because `SET LOCAL` outside a transaction silently no-ops; it caught itself. **Re-check line numbers** — `main` moves, and the hygiene findings in #124 were cited against `99f3151`.
- **Content declared and never read is the majority case:** 11 of 18 room ids, 18 of 20 object ids, 164 of 166 derived locale keys. Never assume a catalog entry has a consumer.
- **ADRs, not implementation decisions.** `CLAUDE.md` requires an ADR when an architectural decision is genuinely absent. Several are `Proposed` and blocked on the owner (#118 has the queue). Do not quietly decide them in code — and note #117: **two Accepted ADRs are both numbered 0004**, so confirm the next free number before writing one.

## Environment facts — save yourself the rediscovery

- Node 24.19 + pnpm 11.22. Baseline on `main`: **121 test files / 1162 passed / 1 skipped**. `npx vitest run`, `npx tsc -b --pretty false`.
- **`git-lfs` is NOT installed**, so `public/assets/**/*.png` are 131-byte pointer files, and **exactly one** browser test fails because of it: "every runtime atlas reaches the page over HTTP and decodes at its authored size" in `tests/browser/app-shell.spec.ts`. **That single failure IS the baseline.** Never try to fix it.
- Browser suite: `LOCKSTATE_BROWSER_TEST_PORT=<port> npx playwright test --config tests/browser/playwright.config.ts`. `strictPort` is set and the config refuses to reuse a server, so **concurrent runs need distinct ports**. If `pnpm exec` fails with `ERR_PNPM_UNSAFE_MODULES_DIR` because `node_modules` is a symlink, set `PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false` — do not edit the config.
- **Known pre-existing flake:** `tests/unit/prisoners-operations-scenario.test.ts` "an identical seed and scenario produce an identical fingerprint" needs ~6 s under CPU load against `vitest.config.ts:14`'s `testTimeout: 5_000`. Passes in isolation, **fails on `main` too**. It matters because a timeout inside a determinism test reads as a *determinism failure* — the most alarming possible false positive here.
- Git worktrees work well. Symlink `node_modules` to `/home/user/lockstate/node_modules` rather than installing per worktree.
- **A local PostgreSQL 16 with pgTAP is available**, superuser as role `root`. That is what made the executed audit in #105 possible — use it rather than reasoning about SQL.
- If you run parallel agents: the workflow concurrency cap is `min(16, CPUs − 2)` and the container has 4 CPUs, so **2 agents per workflow**. Launch multiple workflows to get more in flight.
- **The container is ephemeral.** Anything not on GitHub is lost when it is reclaimed. Write findings to issues *as you go*, not at the end — that is why #124 and #125 exist.
- The owner runs git from Windows and Node only under WSL **on their own machine** (#95); that does not apply to this container.

## Style the owner has asked for, explicitly

**Maximum detail in issues. Spell audits out as thoroughly as possible.** Every claim carries `path:line` **and** the quoted code; VERIFIED versus INFERRED marked explicitly; LIVE versus LATENT stated with what would make a latent one live; the smallest correct fix; whether it needs an ADR or a product decision rather than an implementation choice; the test that should have caught it and the concrete surviving mutation; and any open PR branch touching the same files. **Longer is better.** Do not pad with invention — omit an empty section instead.

Prefer small PRs tied to issues. End GitHub issue bodies and comments with the Claude Code attribution footer. **Never** put a model identifier in a commit message, PR body, or code comment.

---

# Issue map

**Entry points:** **#116** (this) · **#107** handover · **#95** earlier handover (topology, secrets)

**Live defects:** **#115** cursor offset · **#102** `chunkSize` unbounded (429-byte save → 1.6 GB, 24-million-fold amplification) · **#103** restore failure never demoted + worker permanently faulted with a misleading 15 s timeout · **#108** newest build gesture never in the save · **#109** restored-scope sentence is a module constant

**Latent — become live when a destroy/release path exists (#31):** **#110** `EntityStore.isAlive` ignores the `alive` array · **#111** `admitPrisoner` initialises 5 of 18 component arrays

**Determinism:** **#112** `TopologyManager` never resets `nextGlobalId`; asks for ADR 0012 to be Accepted

**Test quality:** **#113** nine `ConstructionSystem` mutations survive the whole suite

**Security:** **#105** the executed migration-by-migration audit — what is cleared, what is not, and what it does not cover · **#106** trusted envelope aliases the caller's objects

**Records, not work:** **#114** a refutation — do **not** "fix" it

**Unapplied review findings:** **#125** for the #88, #92 and #93 branches

**Hygiene:** **#117** duplicate ADR 0004 · **#118** four ADR statuses contradict the code, plus the owner's approval queue · **#119** README claims all ADRs are accepted · **#120** `WORLD.md` states the renderer's rule as the simulation's · **#121** five false doc claims · **#122** two docs contradict themselves · **#123** four rules with two implementations each · **#124** the remainder: CI gates weaker than they look, dead code, archive candidates, AGENTS.md violations, tests that cannot fail

**Product direction:** **#96** money-primary · **#99** dismantle-to-salvage · **#104** the projection channel (four independent analyses converged on this as highest value-per-effort) · **#29** economy · **#78–#81** prisoners

**Open PRs:** **#97** (materials vocabulary + refund, split from #91) · **#98** (deploy step could not fail) · **#100** (deploy after CI — read the risk note above) · **#101** (`verify:sql` before migrations) · **#94** (HUD clock, review fixes applied) · **#91** (starting stock, **held by owner decision**)

items.title: `Undo` and `Redo` have no pointer or touch route at all — the two commands the repository's own comment says a touch player must not be left without
items.body:
Found by the reachability gate merged as #1349 (`tests/foundation/command-control-reachability-contract.test.ts` + `tests/helpers/control-reachability.ts`), and verified first-hand against `main` at `7285e1c4` before this was written. The gate records the pair on `NO_CONTROL_ISSUES_IT` rather than fixing it, because fixing it means putting a control on the HUD and that spends a budget which is at zero. This issue is the fix's brief, not the fix.

## 1. What is true, verified

**The only dispatch is a computed-kind one in `src/ui/hud/hud.ts`**, and its own comment says there is no control behind it:

```ts
  /**
   * The undo and redo keys, joined to the same gate (#261).
   *
   * ...
   * No control is passed, for the reason the gesture above passes none: the
   * player pressed a key on the world, not a button in the HUD, so there is
   * nothing on screen for a refusal to be marked on. The refusal line still
   * says what happened.
   */
  options.editHistory?.attachHistory((direction) => {
    dispatchCommand({ kind: direction });
  });
```

**The chain behind `attachHistory` is a keyboard binding and nothing else.** `src/ui/build-tool.ts` exposes `undo()`/`redo()`, which call `this.history?.('undo')` / `this.history?.('redo')`; the only caller of either in `src/` is `src/rendering/scene/world-scene.ts`'s action switch:

```ts
        /*
         * Reported, not performed. Undo reverses a *simulation* transaction --
         * the orders a gesture placed -- and `src/rendering/` may not submit a
         * command (`tests/unit/rendering-module-boundaries.test.ts`). What
         * belongs here is the half nothing else can do: recognising the key in
         * the `world` context and not in `text-entry` (#261).
         */
        case 'edit.undo':
          this.editHistory?.undo();
          break;
        case 'edit.redo':
          this.editHistory?.redo();
          break;
```

and the two actions have exactly two bindings, both keyboard:

```ts
  { device: 'keyboard', code: 'KeyZ', action: 'edit.undo', contexts: ['world', 'construction'] },
  { device: 'keyboard', code: 'KeyY', action: 'edit.redo', contexts: ['world', 'construction'] },
```

**And the irony the gate reports is real.** `hud.ts` gives exactly this defect as the reason the `RemoveObject` intent exists, in the docblock over `{ readonly kind: 'remove-object'; ... }`:

> **Why this exists at all**, since `Undo` already took a placement back: undo is bound to `KeyZ` and nothing else, so on a touch device a misplaced object was permanent for the session. That is the trap the Rooms tab shipped with and had to fix in a follow-up, and it is not worth repeating.

The trap was named, one command was given a pointer route because of it, and the history pair itself was left where it was.

## 2. The negative half, checked where it applies rather than asserted

The claim "there is genuinely no pointer route" was checked in four places, not one:

1. **The HUD.** `grep -rn "kind: 'undo'\|kind: 'redo'\|attachHistory" src/` returns the declaration in the `HudIntent` union, the `HudEditHistory.attachHistory` signature, the one dispatch quoted above, and `build-tool.ts`. No panel, no row, no button.
2. **The world canvas.** `src/input/pointer.ts`'s `PointerInputAdapter` is the whole of the pointer-to-action path and it does not read the binding table at all. Its `primaryAction()` can return exactly `'build.confirm'` (construction context) or `'selection.primary'` (world context), and `pointerCancel` can emit `'build.cancel'`. There is no branch by which a pointer event becomes `edit.undo`.
3. **The binding table.** `src/input/bindings.ts` holds 13 binding entries and every single one reads `device: 'keyboard'`. That is not a coincidence of the current table: the record type declares the field as the literal `readonly device: 'keyboard';`, so a pointer binding is not something nobody has written yet — it is something the vocabulary cannot express. A remap cannot add one either.
4. **`tests/`, as well as `src/`.** The only non-keyboard producer anywhere is `tests/browser/ui-harness.ts`'s `attachHistory` stub, reached from `window.lockstateUiHarness.pressWorldUndo(...)` in `tests/browser/ui-shell.spec.ts`. That is a test harness calling the seam directly, not a control.

No context menu, no gesture handler, no long-press: `pointer-gesture.ts` recognises pan/pinch/drag and nothing named `undo`.

**So a touch player cannot undo anything, and cannot redo anything.** `AGENTS.md` boundary 10 — *"Input must support remapping, QWERTY/AZERTY and touch/pointer interaction"* — is unmet for these two commands specifically.

## 3. Why this is filed rather than fixed: the budget

`docs/adr/drafts/what-an-action-column-is-and-whether-a-message-can-carry-a-next-step.md` measures both HUD budgets. Its §5a is titled *"Vertical: real, zero-sum, and already spent"* and concludes:

> **So the vertical budget is genuinely at zero, and every option in §6 is measured against it.**

**How much of that draft actually bears on this issue, stated rather than borrowed.** The draft is about an action on an *alert row*, so its two halves do not transfer equally:

- **§5a (vertical) transfers directly to any shape that adds a rail row or a navigation section.** The priced entries are the ones a new undo section would spend: one band row costs `.hud__rail` 35px measured at 900x600; `navigationRailBlock` is `(HUD_TAB_IDS.length * 47 + 24) * scale`, so a seventh section is 47 CSS px at 100 % and 94 at 200 %; the sixth section already collided with `.hud-zoom__in` at 1280x800, and the repair that tried to pay for it out of the corner cost the alerts list 27px and was reverted. Its Option C is therefore dead for an undo section for exactly the reasons it is dead for a messages section.
- **§5b (horizontal) does *not* transfer as a number.** Its 2px margin is the alert row's inside `.hud__corner`, bought by the owner's 2026-09-01 ruling at a 396px floor. An undo control does not go on an alert row, so that specific floor is not the one it spends. What transfers is the *method* and one hard fact: `.hud__corner` is `display: none` below 720px (§5c), so **any shape placed in the corner reaches no phone at all**, which is the one viewport class this issue is most about.
- **§5c is the sharpest thing the draft says about this issue.** The player who cannot undo is the touch player, and the corner — the HUD's only spare horizontal real estate — does not exist for them.

The budget that a realistic shape spends is therefore the **status strip's**, and that one is already over: #719 measures a fully badged row at **1627px against 1256px at 1280x800**, 6 of 9 chips on screen, and prices letting the metrics row wrap at *"a third strip row, ~30px of world height"* against a Build panel whose always-visible budget at 1280x720 is **8px**.

None of that is a reason to leave a command unreachable on touch. It is the reason the shape is a decision and not an implementation detail.

## 4. Two candidate shapes, with what each costs. Not a recommendation — deliberately no choice is made here

### Shape 1 — an Undo/Redo pair in the status strip's transport cluster

Two icon buttons in `.hud-strip__transport` (`src/ui/hud/status-strip.ts`), beside Pause/Play/speed. They are chrome controls about "the last thing I did", which is the same register as the transport, and the strip is present at every viewport including 375x812 — so unlike the corner it reaches the player who needs it.

**Cost.** Horizontal, in the one row that is already measured over budget. Two controls at `--tap-target` (`calc(44px * var(--ui-scale))`) is **88px at 100 % and 176px at 200 %**, added to a row that #719 measures at 1627px of content against 1256px of room at 1280x800 in the fully badged state. `.hud-strip__transport` declares `gap: var(--space-1)` and the strip's slot is `flex: none` with `flex-wrap: wrap`, so what gives is not the transport controls but a **wrap to a second strip row** at the viewports where it triggers — the strip's own comment prices that as *"one row of strip height at the viewports where it triggers"*, and #719 route 2 prices the same thing as ~30px of world height against the Build panel's 8px. **Vertical grid cost: zero** — no new rail row, no change to `navigationRailBlock`.

**What it forecloses / what it needs measured before it is taken.** Whether the strip wraps at 1280x720 with the pair present and an ordinary populated prison (#719's *un*-badged measurement is 1238px in 1256px, so 88px more wraps it — this needs the actual measurement, not this arithmetic). Whether it interacts with #719's own open copy decision, since shortening the coverage badge would free 140px and change the answer.

### Shape 2 — an Undo/Redo pair inside the Build and Rooms panels, beside the tool arm

Two controls in the panel body — `src/ui/hud/build-panel.ts` and `src/ui/hud/rooms-panel.ts` — next to the arm/stand-down control, where the gesture that gets undone was made.

**Cost.** Vertical, inside `.ui-panel.hud-build` / `.ui-panel.hud-rooms`. **No grid cost at all**: `mountHud` shows exactly one of Build, Rooms, Staff and Intake in `.hud__side`, and the panels are their own scroll containers, which is the argument `staff-panel.ts` already makes for the held-guards block (*"what the rail cannot give it is its own to scroll"*). The price is paid in the fold instead: the Build panel's body already spills past its box at all five viewports — measured in the sweep at **179px at 1280x720, 44 at 1440x900, 143 at 1024x768, 151 at 900x600 and 160 at 375x812** — so a row added above the fold pushes something below it, and `staff-panel.ts`'s own measurement of a fourth held row (*"A fourth row puts its Release 9.0px below that fold"*) is the shape of the failure to avoid.

**What it forecloses.** Undo is bound in the `world` **and** `construction` contexts and reverses a construction transaction whoever is looking at whatever tab; a control that exists only on two of the six tabs (`HUD_TAB_IDS` is `overview, build, zones, manage, day-plan, security`) is narrower than the key it is standing in for, and a player who placed a wall and then switched to Manage has no way back. It also duplicates the control, so the two copies must not disagree about enablement.

### A third shape, named because it is what a reader proposes first, and it is refuted

**A long-press or two-finger gesture on the world canvas.** It cannot satisfy the property this issue is about. `app-shell.spec.ts`'s `INTERACTIVE_SELECTOR` is `button, [role="button"], a[href], input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`, and #1349's walk reports a producer that bottoms out on anything else as `'non-interactive'` — which is precisely the defect #903 fixed on the minimap surface after ten months. A gesture would give a touch player undo and would leave it invisible to both the #88 sweep and the reachability gate, and the gate would go red naming it. It is also the arrangement the constitution's article 7 constrains (*"Przesunięcie kamery i zlecenie budowy nie mogą wynikać z tego samego gestu"*).

## 5. What "done" looks like

`NO_CONTROL_ISSUES_IT` in `tests/foundation/command-control-reachability-contract.test.ts` loses both entries in the same change that adds the control — the gate's `holds no entry for a command that has since gained a control` case already fails if an entry outlives the fact — and the `measures sixteen commands with a control, two with none` case's denominators move from 16/2 to 18/0.
